 《[爸爸来了](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E7%88%B8%E7%88%B8%E6%9D%A5%E4%BA%86&action=edit&redlink=1 "爸爸来了（页面不存在）")（英语：[There Comes Papa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There_Comes_Papa "en:There Comes Papa")）》（1893），描绘了瓦尔马的女儿马哈普拉巴（Mahaprabha）及其一个儿子。

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg/250px-Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_(1848%E2%80%931901).jpg)

 瓦尔马的大姨子[巴拉尼·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%B7%B4%E6%8B%89%E5%B0%BC%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "巴拉尼·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "en:Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi")）是[阿特廷格阿尔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%98%BF%E7%89%B9%E5%BB%B7%E6%A0%BC%E9%98%BF%E5%B0%94 "阿特廷格阿尔")（或特拉凡哥尔）的大拉尼（Senior Rani），她在1900年收养了瓦尔马的两个外孙女。

拉维·瓦尔马的母亲乌玛·安巴巴伊·坦普拉蒂（Uma Ambabayi Thampuratty）属于男爵家族，该家族统治着特拉凡哥尔王国内的基利马诺尔[封建庄园](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A2%86%E5%9C%B0 "领地")。她是一位颇有才华的诗人和作家，她的作品《帕尔瓦蒂·斯瓦亚姆瓦兰》（Parvati Swayamvaram）在其死后由瓦尔马出版。拉维·瓦尔马的父亲埃祖马维尔·尼拉坎坦·巴塔蒂里帕德（Ezhumavil Neelakanthan Bhattatiripad）是[梵语](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%A2%B5%E8%AF%AD "梵语")和[阿育吠陀](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%98%BF%E8%82%B2%E5%90%A0%E9%99%80 "阿育吠陀")学者，来自喀拉拉邦的[埃尔纳古勒姆](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%9F%83%E5%B0%94%E7%BA%B3%E5%8F%A4%E5%8B%92%E5%A7%86 "埃尔纳古勒姆")。拉维·瓦尔马姊妹三人，有一个弟弟名叫[C·拉贾·拉贾·瓦尔马](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&redlink=1 "C·拉贾·拉贾·瓦尔马（页面不存在）")（英语：[C. Raja Raja Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Raja_Raja_Varma "en:C. Raja Raja Varma")）（生于1860年），还有一个妹妹名叫[曼加拉·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%9B%BC%E5%8A%A0%E6%8B%89%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "曼加拉·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Mangala Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangala_Bayi "en:Mangala Bayi")）。他弟弟也是一位画家，一生都与拉维·瓦尔马密切合作。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

1866年，18岁的瓦尔马被[包办婚姻](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8C%85%E5%8A%9E%E5%A9%9A%E5%A7%BB "包办婚姻")，娶了12岁的巴吉尔蒂·巴伊（Bhageerthi Bayi，全名普鲁鲁塔蒂·纳尔·巴吉尔蒂·巴伊·坦普拉蒂 (Pooruruttati Nal Bhageerathi Bayi Thampuratty)），她是特拉凡哥尔王国另一个主要[封地](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A2%86%E5%9C%B0 "领地")[马韦利克卡拉](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A9%AC%E9%9F%A6%E5%88%A9%E5%85%8B%E5%8D%A1%E6%8B%89 "马韦利克卡拉")的王室成员。值得注意的是，马韦利克卡拉王室是特拉凡哥尔王室的一个分支。巴吉尔蒂是姐妹三人中最小的一个，她的两个姐姐都于1857年被特拉凡哥尔王室收养，以延续血统。她们被称为阿特廷格阿尔的大小拉尼（Rani），她们的后代获得了特拉凡哥尔王位的继承权。因为拉维·瓦尔马与巴吉尔蒂的婚姻，他与王室的关系变得非常密切。他的孩子（因为他们属于母亲的家族）出生时就是皇室成员。这场婚姻是由父母以印度人特有的方式安排的，但和谐而成功。夫妇俩共有五个孩子，两儿三女。他们的大儿子喀拉拉·瓦尔马（Kerala Varma，1876年出生）患有精神疾病。他终生未婚，并最终于1912年自杀。小儿子拉马·瓦尔马（Rama Varma，1879年出生）继承了父亲的艺术天赋，就读于[孟买](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%AD%9F%E4%B9%B0 "孟买")[J·J爵士应用艺术学院](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=J%C2%B7J%E7%88%B5%E5%A3%AB%E5%BA%94%E7%94%A8%E8%89%BA%E6%9C%AF%E5%AD%A6%E9%99%A2&action=edit&redlink=1 "J·J爵士应用艺术学院（页面不存在）")（英语：[Sir J.J. Institute of Applied Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_J.J._Institute_of_Applied_Art "en:Sir J.J. Institute of Applied Art")）。他娶了[德万](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%BE%B7%E4%B8%87&action=edit&redlink=1 "德万（页面不存在）")（英语：[Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "en:Dewan")）的妹妹（或姐姐）高里·昆贾玛（Gowri Kunjamma），并生育了七个孩子。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

拉维·瓦尔马和巴吉尔蒂·巴伊的三个女儿是马哈普拉巴·阿马（Mahaprabha Amma，她出现在瓦尔马两幅最著名的画作中）、乌玛·阿马（Uma Amma，随了瓦尔马母亲的名字）和切里亚·科查马（Cheria Kochamma）。公元1900年，特拉凡哥尔王室再次面临继任危机。为了继承血统，巴吉尔蒂的两个姐姐被王室收养，但她们均未能如愿产下继承人。她们共有六个孩子，但只有两个存活下来，而且都是男孩（他们后来也意外去世而未留子嗣）。根据[玛鲁玛卡塔亚姆](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E7%8E%9B%E9%B2%81%E7%8E%9B%E5%8D%A1%E5%A1%94%E4%BA%9A%E5%A7%86&action=edit&redlink=1 "玛鲁玛卡塔亚姆（页面不存在）")（英语：[Marumakkathayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marumakkathayam "en:Marumakkathayam")）[母系制度](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%AF%8D%E7%B3%BB%E5%88%B6%E5%BA%A6 "母系制度")，只能通过女性来继承王位，所以必须要进行收养。根据传统，会同时收养王室分支的两个女孩。根据不寻常且独特的玛鲁玛卡塔亚姆继承制度，她们会被指定为阿特廷格阿尔的大小拉尼，并将特拉凡哥尔的王位继承权赋予他们的后代。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

瓦尔马的两个外孙女注定要获得这一荣誉，主要原因是她们是现任阿特廷格阿尔的拉尼最近的母系（[同族](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%90%8C%E6%97%8F%E4%BA%B2%E5%B1%9E&action=edit&redlink=1 "同族亲属（页面不存在）")（英语：[Cognatic kinship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognatic_kinship "en:Cognatic kinship")））亲属。1900年8月，马哈普拉巴的长女拉克希米·巴伊（Lakshmi Bayi，5岁）和乌玛的长女帕尔瓦蒂·巴伊（Parvati Bayi，4岁）被特拉凡哥尔王室收养。正式收养她们的是她们仍在世的外祖母[巴拉尼·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%B7%B4%E6%8B%89%E5%B0%BC%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "巴拉尼·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "en:Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi")）。收养后不到一年她就去世了，然后这两个女孩分别被任命为阿特廷格阿尔的大小拉尼。她们在十四五岁的时候就嫁给了两位门当户对的贵族家庭的绅士。1912年，小拉尼[塞图·帕尔瓦蒂·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%A1%9E%E5%9B%BE%C2%B7%E5%B8%95%E5%B0%94%E7%93%A6%E8%92%82%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "塞图·帕尔瓦蒂·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Sethu Parvathi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Parvathi_Bayi "en:Sethu Parvathi Bayi")）生下了期待已久的继承人，那天刚好是她16岁生日的第二天。巧合的是，她丈夫是拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马的侄孙，属于基利马诺尔。这个婴儿就是后来的大君[奇提拉·蒂鲁纳尔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%A5%87%E6%8F%90%E6%8B%89%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E6%8B%89%E6%8B%89%E9%A9%AC%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&redlink=1 "奇提拉·蒂鲁纳尔·巴拉拉马·瓦尔马（页面不存在）")（英语：[Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chithira_Thirunal_Balarama_Varma "en:Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma")），也是最后一位[特拉凡哥尔大君](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E7%89%B9%E6%8B%89%E5%87%A1%E5%93%A5%E5%B0%94%E5%A4%A7%E5%90%9B%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8&action=edit&redlink=1 "特拉凡哥尔大君列表（页面不存在）")（英语：[List of Maharajas of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Maharajas_of_Travancore "en:List of Maharajas of Travancore")）。他下面还有一个弟弟（后来的大君马尔坦达·瓦尔马三世）和一个妹妹[卡尔西卡·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8D%A1%E5%B0%94%E8%A5%BF%E5%8D%A1%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "卡尔西卡·蒂鲁纳尔·拉克希米·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Karthika Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karthika_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "en:Karthika Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi")）。卡尔西卡·蒂鲁纳尔是拉马·瓦尔马七世的母亲，而拉马·瓦尔马七世就是自2013年起在位的大君。同时，大拉尼（[塞图·拉克希米·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%A1%9E%E5%9B%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "塞图·拉克希米·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Sethu Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Lakshmi_Bayi "en:Sethu Lakshmi Bayi")），马哈普拉巴·阿马的女儿，1924至1931年摄政）也在1923和1926年生下两个女儿。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

因此，特拉凡哥尔现有的整个王室都是拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马的后裔。在其皇室后裔中，出名的有作家[阿斯瓦蒂·蒂鲁纳尔·高里·拉克希米·巴伊](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%98%BF%E6%96%AF%E7%93%A6%E8%92%82%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E9%AB%98%E9%87%8C%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E5%B7%B4%E4%BC%8A&action=edit&redlink=1 "阿斯瓦蒂·蒂鲁纳尔·高里·拉克希米·巴伊（页面不存在）")（英语：[Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Gowri_Lakshmi_Bayi "en:Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi")）和[史瑞库马尔·瓦尔马](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8F%B2%E7%91%9E%E5%BA%93%E9%A9%AC%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&redlink=1 "史瑞库马尔·瓦尔马（页面不存在）")（英语：[Shreekumar Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreekumar_Varma "en:Shreekumar Varma")）、艺术家[鲁米尼·瓦尔马](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%B2%81%E7%B1%B3%E5%B0%BC%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&redlink=1 "鲁米尼·瓦尔马（页面不存在）")（英语：[Rukmini Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rukmini_Varma "en:Rukmini Varma")）和古典音乐家[阿斯瓦蒂·蒂鲁纳尔·拉马·瓦尔马](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%98%BF%E6%96%AF%E7%93%A6%E8%92%82%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E9%A9%AC%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&redlink=1 "阿斯瓦蒂·蒂鲁纳尔·拉马·瓦尔马（页面不存在）")（英语：[Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "en:Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma")）。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

在拉维·瓦尔马57岁生日前后，他宣布决定接受三亚撒（Sanyasa），并在60岁时退休。在他生命的最后几年，他因拉贾·拉贾·瓦尔马（Raja Raja Varma）的去世而悲痛不已，也忍受着糖尿病的痛苦，并因此于1906年10月2日去世。[[7]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-7)

## 艺术生涯

[[编辑](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&section=2 "编辑章节：艺术生涯")]

瓦尔马曾受到下一任特拉凡哥尔大君[艾伊利亚姆·蒂鲁纳尔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E8%89%BE%E4%BC%8A%E5%88%A9%E4%BA%9A%E5%A7%86%C2%B7%E8%92%82%E9%B2%81%E7%BA%B3%E5%B0%94&action=edit&redlink=1 "艾伊利亚姆·蒂鲁纳尔（页面不存在）")（英语：[Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "en:Ayilyam Thirunal")）的光顾，并从此后开始接受正式培训。[[8]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-The_Diary_of_C._Rajaraja_Varma-8)他在[马杜赖](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A9%AC%E6%9D%9C%E8%B5%96 "马杜赖")学习了绘画的基础知识。后来，他接受了拉马·斯瓦米·奈杜（Rama Swami Naidu）的水彩画培训，并勉强接受了英国肖像画家西奥多·詹森（Theodore Jenson）的[油画](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%B2%B9%E7%94%BB "油画")培训。[[9]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-9)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg)

 瓦尔马住在[拉克希米·维拉斯宫](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E7%BB%B4%E6%8B%89%E6%96%AF%E5%AE%AB&action=edit&redlink=1 "拉克希米·维拉斯宫（页面不存在）")（英语：[Lakshmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshmi_Vilas_Palace,_Vadodara "en:Lakshmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara")）期间使用的工作室

英国行政官[埃德加·瑟斯顿](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%9F%83%E5%BE%B7%E5%8A%A0%C2%B7%E7%91%9F%E6%96%AF%E9%A1%BF&action=edit&redlink=1 "埃德加·瑟斯顿（页面不存在）")（英语：[Edgar Thurston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Thurston "en:Edgar Thurston")）在推动瓦尔马和他弟弟的事业方面发挥了重要作用。[[10]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-10)瓦尔马于1873年在[维也纳](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%BB%B4%E4%B9%9F%E7%BA%B3 "维也纳")举办了画展并获奖，之后获得了广泛赞誉。瓦尔马的画作还被送往1893年的[芝加哥哥伦布纪念博览会](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%8A%9D%E5%8A%A0%E5%93%A5%E5%93%A5%E4%BC%A6%E5%B8%83%E7%BA%AA%E5%BF%B5%E5%8D%9A%E8%A7%88%E4%BC%9A "芝加哥哥伦布纪念博览会")，并获得了三枚金奖。[[11]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-11)他走遍印度，寻找主题。他经常以他认为美丽的[印度](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E5%8D%97%E9%83%A8 "印度南部")女性作为[印度教](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E6%95%99 "印度教")[女神](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A5%B3%E7%A5%9E "女神")的模特。拉维·瓦尔马特别出名的绘画题材是，描绘《[摩诃婆罗多](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%91%A9%E8%AF%83%E5%A9%86%E7%BD%97%E5%A4%9A "摩诃婆罗多")》中[杜尚塔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%9D%9C%E5%B0%9A%E5%A1%94&action=edit&redlink=1 "杜尚塔（页面不存在）")（英语：[Dushyanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushyanta "en:Dushyanta")）和[沙昆塔拉](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%B2%99%E6%98%86%E5%A1%94%E6%8B%89&action=edit&redlink=1 "沙昆塔拉（页面不存在）")（英语：[Shakuntala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakuntala "en:Shakuntala")），以及[那拉](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%82%A3%E6%8B%89_(%E6%91%A9%E8%AF%83%E5%A9%86%E7%BD%97%E5%A4%9A)&action=edit&redlink=1 "那拉 (摩诃婆罗多)（页面不存在）")（英语：[Nala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nala "en:Nala")）和[达马扬蒂](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E8%BE%BE%E9%A9%AC%E6%89%AC%E8%92%82&action=edit&redlink=1 "达马扬蒂（页面不存在）")（英语：[Damayanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damayanti "en:Damayanti")）的故事情节。拉维·瓦尔马所表现的[神话](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E8%AF%9D "神话")人物，已经成为印度史诗想象的一部分。他经常因风格过于浮夸和感伤而受到批评，但其作品在印度仍然很受欢迎。他的许多精美画作都收藏在[拉克希米·维拉斯宫](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E5%85%8B%E5%B8%8C%E7%B1%B3%C2%B7%E7%BB%B4%E6%8B%89%E6%96%AF%E5%AE%AB&action=edit&redlink=1 "拉克希米·维拉斯宫（页面不存在）")（英语：[Lakshmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshmi_Vilas_Palace,_Vadodara "en:Lakshmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara")）。[[12]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-12)

## 拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马出版社

[[编辑](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&section=3 "编辑章节：拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马出版社")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_Mrs._Ramanadha_Rao.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_Mrs._Ramanadha_Rao.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma,_Mrs._Ramanadha_Rao.jpg)

 《拉马纳达·饶夫人和儿子》（Mrs. Ramanadha Rao and son）

显然是在特拉凡哥尔当时的德万（总理）[T·玛达瓦·饶](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=T%C2%B7%E7%8E%9B%E8%BE%BE%E7%93%A6%C2%B7%E9%A5%B6&action=edit&redlink=1 "T·玛达瓦·饶（页面不存在）")（英语：[T. Madhava Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._Madhava_Rao "en:T. Madhava Rao")）的建议下，拉维·瓦尔马于1894年在孟买的[加特科帕尔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8A%A0%E7%89%B9%E7%A7%91%E5%B8%95%E5%B0%94&action=edit&redlink=1 "加特科帕尔（页面不存在）")（英语：[Ghatkopar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghatkopar "en:Ghatkopar")）开设了一间石版印刷出版社，后于1899年将其转移到[马哈拉施特拉邦](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%A9%AC%E5%93%88%E6%8B%89%E6%96%BD%E7%89%B9%E6%8B%89%E9%82%A6 "马哈拉施特拉邦")[洛纳瓦拉](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%B4%9B%E7%BA%B3%E7%93%A6%E6%8B%89 "洛纳瓦拉")附近的[马拉夫利](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%A9%AC%E6%8B%89%E5%A4%AB%E5%88%A9&action=edit&redlink=1 "马拉夫利（页面不存在）")（英语：[Malavli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malavli "en:Malavli")）。该出版社制作的[版画](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BD%A9%E8%89%B2%E5%B9%B3%E7%89%88%E5%8D%B0%E5%88%B7%E8%A1%93 "彩色平版印刷術")内容大多是印度教各神祗，其场景主要改编自《[摩诃婆罗多](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%91%A9%E8%AF%83%E5%A9%86%E7%BD%97%E5%A4%9A "摩诃婆罗多")》、《[罗摩衍那](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%BD%97%E6%91%A9%E8%A1%8D%E9%82%A3 "罗摩衍那")》和《[往世书](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%BE%80%E4%B8%96%E4%B9%A6 "往世书")》。这些版画非常受欢迎，多年来一直持续印刷了数千张，甚至一直持续到1906年拉维·瓦尔马去世之后。[[來源請求]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:%E5%88%97%E6%98%8E%E6%9D%A5%E6%BA%90 "Wikipedia:列明来源")

拉维·瓦尔马出版社是当时印度最大、最具创新性的出版社。该出版社由拉维的弟弟拉贾·瓦尔马管理，但在他们的管理下，商业上不太成功。到1899年，出版社负债累累；1901年，出版社被卖给了他来自德国的印刷技术员弗里茨·施莱歇尔（Fritz Schleicher）。施莱歇尔继续印刷拉维·瓦尔马的版画，但后来聘请了其他艺术家创作新的设计。施莱歇尔还扩大了出版社的产品范围，引入了商业和广告标签。在施莱歇尔及其继任者的管理下，出版社一直很成功。但1972年的毁灭性火灾烧毁了整个工厂。拉维·瓦尔马的许多原始平版印刷品也在大火中毁于一旦。[[13]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-13)

## 荣誉

[[编辑](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&section=4 "编辑章节：荣誉")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg?utm_source=zh.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg)

 1971年印度邮票上的拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马

1904年，总督寇松勋爵代表英皇授予瓦尔马[凯撒-艾-欣德勋章](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%87%AF%E6%92%92-%E8%89%BE-%E6%AC%A3%E5%BE%B7%E5%8B%8B%E7%AB%A0&action=edit&redlink=1 "凯撒-艾-欣德勋章（页面不存在）")（英语：[Kaisar-i-Hind Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaisar-i-Hind_Medal "en:Kaisar-i-Hind Medal")）。为了纪念他，在喀拉拉邦的马韦利克卡拉还成立了一所[美术](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%BE%8E%E6%9C%AF "美术")学院。基利马诺尔的拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马高中是以他的名字命名的，印度各地还有许多文化组织都以他的名字命名。2013年，以他的名字命名了[水星](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%B0%B4%E6%98%9F "水星")上的瓦尔马陨石坑。[[14]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-14)考虑到他对[印度艺术](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E8%97%9D%E8%A1%93 "印度藝術")的巨大贡献，喀拉拉邦政府设立了[拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马奖](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC%E5%A5%96&action=edit&redlink=1 "拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马奖（页面不存在）")（英语：[Raja Ravi Varma Puraskaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma_Puraskaram "en:Raja Ravi Varma Puraskaram")），每年颁发给在艺术和文化领域表现卓越的人。[[15]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-15)

*   在他逝世65周年之际，[印度邮政](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8D%B0%E5%BA%A6%E9%82%AE%E6%94%BF&action=edit&redlink=1 "印度邮政（页面不存在）")（英语：[India Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Post "en:India Post")）发行了一枚纪念邮票，描绘了拉维·瓦尔马和他的名画《达马扬蒂与天鹅》（Damayanti and Swan）。

## 评价

[[编辑](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC&action=edit&section=5 "编辑章节：评价")]

拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马有时被认为是印度第一位现代艺术家，因为他能够将西方美学与印度肖像学相结合。印度艺术史学家和评论家[吉塔·卡普尔](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%90%89%E5%A1%94%C2%B7%E5%8D%A1%E6%99%AE%E5%B0%94&action=edit&redlink=1 "吉塔·卡普尔（页面不存在）")（英语：[Geeta Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Kapur "en:Geeta Kapur")）写道：

> 拉维·瓦尔马是无可争议的印度现代艺术之父。他既天真又雄心勃勃，为后来的同胞展开了一些具体问题的辩论，如：通过专业敏锐度来定义个人天才，测试具有特殊效果的文化适应模式，尝试历史角度的图画叙述等。[[16]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-16)

同样，[巴罗达大学](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B7%B4%E7%BD%97%E8%BE%BE%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6 "巴罗达大学")的艺术家[古拉姆·穆罕默德·谢赫](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8F%A4%E6%8B%89%E5%A7%86%C2%B7%E7%A9%86%E7%BD%95%E9%BB%98%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E8%B0%A2%E8%B5%AB&action=edit&redlink=1 "古拉姆·穆罕默德·谢赫（页面不存在）")（英语：[Gulam Mohammed Sheikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulam_Mohammed_Sheikh "en:Gulam Mohammed Sheikh")）也将拉维·瓦尔马描述为现代艺术家。在他的文章《拉维·瓦尔马在巴罗达》（Ravi Varma in Baroda）中，谢赫将瓦尔马称为建立印度现代艺术的关键人物，并说道：“印度当代艺术的故事，在拉维·瓦尔马进入后，就再也不一样了。他几乎在每个方面都留下了自己的印记。”谢赫和卡普尔一样，称赞拉维·瓦尔马对印度与西方的美学与技术的融合，并将他与印度现代主义者[南达拉·玻色](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E5%8D%97%E8%BE%BE%E6%8B%89%C2%B7%E7%8E%BB%E8%89%B2&action=edit&redlink=1 "南达拉·玻色（页面不存在）")（英语：[Nandalal Bose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandalal_Bose "en:Nandalal Bose")）相提并论。[[17]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-17)

然而，对拉维·瓦尔马的评价也存在争议。巴罗达学派艺术家和艺术史学家[拉坦·帕里穆](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%8B%89%E5%9D%A6%C2%B7%E5%B8%95%E9%87%8C%E7%A9%86&action=edit&redlink=1 "拉坦·帕里穆（页面不存在）")（英语：[Ratan Parimoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratan_Parimoo "en:Ratan Parimoo")）对拉维·瓦尔马的评价并不高，贬称他庸俗，并称瓦尔马的作品在精神上不如民间艺术和部落艺术真实。他认为拉维·瓦尔马应对流行艺术的“粗俗”负责，将瓦尔马的作品与日历艺术和电影中流行画面的艳丽色彩和性感相提并论。[[18]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-19)

尽管对拉维·瓦尔马的评价颇具争议，但他仍然是印度现代和当代艺术家的重要人物。例如，现代艺术家[纳里尼·马拉尼](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E7%BA%B3%E9%87%8C%E5%B0%BC%C2%B7%E9%A9%AC%E6%8B%89%E5%B0%BC&action=edit&redlink=1 "纳里尼·马拉尼（页面不存在）")（英语：[Nalini Malani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalini_Malani "en:Nalini Malani")）在其视频装置《求同存异》（Unity in Diversity）中重现了拉维·瓦尔马的《[音乐家银河](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E9%9F%B3%E4%B9%90%E5%AE%B6%E9%93%B6%E6%B2%B3&action=edit&redlink=1 "音乐家银河（页面不存在）")（英语：[Galaxy of Musicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy_of_Musicians "en:Galaxy of Musicians")）》，来质疑拉维·瓦尔马的理想民族主义。[[20]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-20)同样，当代艺术家[普什帕马拉·N](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E6%99%AE%E4%BB%80%E5%B8%95%E9%A9%AC%E6%8B%89%C2%B7N&action=edit&redlink=1 "普什帕马拉·N（页面不存在）")（英语：[Pushpamala N.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushpamala_N. "en:Pushpamala N.")）以自己为主题，重新创作了几幅拉维·瓦尔马的画作，来解构拉维·瓦尔马对女神和印度女人的理想化描绘。

许多组织都通过节目来纪念他，并以他的名义颁奖。每年都会举办为期两天的兰吉辛大君盖克瓦德艺术节（The Maharaja Ranjitsinh Gaekwad Festival of Arts），在[古吉拉特邦](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%8F%A4%E5%90%89%E6%8B%89%E7%89%B9%E9%82%A6 "古吉拉特邦")[巴罗达](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B7%B4%E7%BD%97%E8%BE%BE_(%E5%8F%A4%E5%90%89%E6%8B%89%E7%89%B9%E9%82%A6) "巴罗达 (古吉拉特邦)")拉克希米·维拉斯宫的杜巴大厅（Durbar Hall）纪念他。[[21]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-Sandesh2022-22)视觉艺术领域的拉贾·拉维·瓦尔马卓越奖（Raja Ravi Varma Award for Excellence in the Field of Visual Arts）在该艺术节期间颁发。[贾扬特·帕里克](https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%E8%B4%BE%E6%89%AC%E7%89%B9%C2%B7%E5%B8%95%E9%87%8C%E5%85%8B&action=edit&redlink=1 "贾扬特·帕里克（页面不存在）")（英语：[Jayant Parikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayant_Parikh "en:Jayant Parikh")）是第一个获奖者。[[23]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E8%B4%BE%C2%B7%E6%8B%89%E7%BB%B4%C2%B7%E7%93%A6%E5%B0%94%E9%A9%AC#cite_note-24)

Ravi Varma is the indisputable father figure of modern Indian art. Naive and ambitious at the same time, he opens up the debate for his later compatriots in the specific matter of defining individual genius through professional acumen, of testing modes of cultural adaptation with idiosyncratic effect, of attempting pictorial narration with its historic scope.

Raja Ravi Varma

**Raja Ravi Varma** (29 April 1848 – 2 October 1906) was an Indian painter and artist. His works are one of the best examples of the fusion of European academic art with a purely Indian sensibility and iconography. Especially, he was notable for making affordable lithographs of his paintings available to the public, which greatly enhanced his reach and influence as a painter and public figure. **Raja Ravi Varma** (Malayalam:[[ɾaːd͡ʒaː ɾɐʋi ʋɐrmːɐ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")) (29 April 1848 – 2 October 1906[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-4)) was an Indian painter. His works are one of the best examples of the fusion of European [academic art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_art "Academic art") with a purely Indian sensibility and iconography. He greatly enhanced his reach and influence as a painter and public figure by making affordable [lithographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithography "Lithography") of his paintings available to the public. His lithographs increased the involvement of common people with fine arts and defined artistic tastes. His religious depictions of Hindu deities and works from [Indian epic poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_epic_poetry "Indian epic poetry") and [Puranas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puranas "Puranas") have received critical acclaim. He was part of the royal family of [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad"), [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district").

Raja Ravi Varma was closely related to the royal family of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") of present-day [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") state in India. Later in his life, two of his granddaughters were adopted into the royal family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-5)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Varma was born on 29 April 1848, as [M. R. Ry.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha_Raja_Rajya_Shri "Maha Raja Rajya Shri") Ravi Varma ([Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_language "Malayalam language"): രവി വർമ്മ), [Koil Thampuran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koyi_Thampuran "Koyi Thampuran") of Kilimanoor at [Kilimanoor palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_palace "Kilimanoor palace") in the erstwhile [princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") (present-day [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"))[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-pal-6) into an aristocratic family that for over 200 years produced consorts for the princesses of the matrilineal Travancore royal family. The title [Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja "Raja") was conferred as a personal title by the Viceroy and Governor-General of India [Lord Curzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Curzon "Lord Curzon").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-pal-6)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma,_There_Comes_Papa_(1893).jpg)

[_There comes Papa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There_Comes_Papa "There Comes Papa") (1893), depicting Varma's daughter Mahaprabha with one of her sons

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg/250px-Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_(1848%E2%80%931901).jpg)

Varma's sister-in-law, [Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), Senior Rani of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") (or [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Travancore "Kingdom of Travancore")), who adopted Varma's granddaughters in 1900

Ravi Varma was the son of Ezhumavil Neelakanthan Bhattatiripad and Uma Ambabayi Thampurratti. His mother Uma Ambabayi Thampuratty belonged to the baronial family which ruled the Kilimanoor [feudal estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") within the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). She was a poet and writer, and her work _Parvati Swayamvaram_ was published by Varma after her death. Ravi Varma's father was a scholar of [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") and [Ayurveda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayurveda "Ayurveda") and hailed from the [Ernakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam "Ernakulam") district in Kerala. Ravi Varma had two siblings, a sister named [Mangala Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangala_Bayi "Mangala Bayi") and a brother named [Raja Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Raja_Raja_Varma "C. Raja Raja Varma") (born 1860). The last-named was also a painter and worked closely with Ravi Varma all his life.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1866, at age 18, Varma was married to 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi (known formally as Pooruruttati Nal Bhageerathi Bayi Thampuratty) of the royal house of [Mavelikkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavelikkara "Mavelikkara"), another major [fief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") of Travancore kingdom. Notably, the house of Mavellikara was a branch of the Royal House of Travancore. Bhageerthi was the youngest of three sisters; her two elder siblings were adopted into the royal family of Travancore in 1857 to perpetuate the lineage. Designated the Senior and Junior Rani of Attingal, their descendants were vested with the succession to the throne of Travancore. Therefore, Ravi Varma's connection to the royal family became very close due to his marriage with Bhageerthi. His children would be royal by birth, since they belonged to their mother's family. The marriage, which was arranged by the parents in the proper Indian manner, was considered successful. The couple had five children, two sons, and three daughters. Their elder son, Kerala Varma (b.1876) was of an excessively spiritual temperament. He never married and eventually renounced the world, leaving home for good in 1912. The younger son, Rama Varma (born 1879), inherited his father's artistic talent and studied at the [JJ School of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_School_of_Arts "JJ School of Arts"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). He was married to Gowri Kunjamma, sister of [Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan")[PGN Unnithan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGN_Unnithan "PGN Unnithan"), and became the father of seven children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The three daughters of Ravi Varma and Bhageerthi Bayi were Mahaprabha Amma (who features in two of Varma's most famous paintings), Uma Amma (named after Varma's mother) and Cheria Kochamma. In 1900 CE, the Royal House of Travancore once again faced a succession crisis. Bhageerthi's two elder sisters, who had been adopted in order to carry forward the lineage, had failed to produce the desired heirs. They had six children between them, but only two of those survived, and both were boys (who also, incidentally, later died childless). According to the [matrilineal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrilineal "Matrilineal") Marumakkathayam system, the succession to the throne could only progress through females, and therefore it was necessary to make an adoption. Tradition dictated that two girls belonging to branches of the Royal Family be adopted together. They would be designated the Senior and Junior Rani of Attingal, and the succession to the throne of Travancore would be vested in their progeny, in accordance with the unusual and unique [Marumakkathayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marumakkathayam "Marumakkathayam") system of succession.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Two of Varma's granddaughters were marked by destiny to receive this honour, the main reason being that they were the nearest matrilineal ([cognatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognatic "Cognatic")) kin to the incumbent Rani of Attingal. In August 1900, Mahaprabha's eldest daughter Lakshmi Bayi (aged 5 years) and Uma's eldest daughter Parvati Bayi (aged 4 years) were adopted into the Royal family of Travancore. It was [Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), their surviving grand-aunt, who formally adopted them. She died within one year of doing this, and the two girls were then installed as the Senior and Junior Ranis of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") respectively. They were married while yet in their early teens to two gentlemen from suitable aristocratic families. It was the Junior Rani, [Sethu Parvathi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Parvathi_Bayi "Sethu Parvathi Bayi"), who gave birth to the much-awaited heir in 1912, exactly a day after her sixteenth birthday. Incidentally, her husband was a grand-nephew of Raja Ravi Varma and belonged to [Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_Palace "Kilimanoor Palace"). The newborn child was the future Maharaja [Chithira Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chithira_Thirunal_Balarama_Varma "Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma"), the last ruling [Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Travancore "Maharaja of Travancore"). He was followed by a brother (the future Maharaja [Marthanda Varma III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthradom_Thirunal_Marthanda_Varma "Uthradom Thirunal Marthanda Varma")) and a sister [Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karthika_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Karthika Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), the mother of Maharaja [Rama Varma VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma") who is presently on the throne (since 2013). Meanwhile, the Senior Rani ([Sethu Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Lakshmi_Bayi "Sethu Lakshmi Bayi"), daughter of Mahaprabha Amma, and Regent from 1924 to 1931) also gave birth to two daughters later in life (in 1923 and 1926).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In this way, the entire present (existing) royal family of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") is descended from Raja Ravi Varma. Well known among his royal descendants are the writers [Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Gowri_Lakshmi_Bayi "Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi") and [Shreekumar Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreekumar_Varma "Shreekumar Varma"), the artist [Rukmini Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rukmini_Varma "Rukmini Varma") and the classical musician [Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Around Ravi Varma's 57th birthday he announced his decision to accept [Sanyasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasa "Sanyasa"), and retire from all worldly life when he turned 60. In his final years he suffered from grief for the death of Raja Raja Varma, and also from diabetes, which contributed to his death on 2 October 1906.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Art career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Art career")]

Varma was patronised by [Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal"), the next [Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Travancore "Maharaja of Travancore") and began formal training thereafter.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-The_Diary_of_C._Rajaraja_Varma-7) He learned the basics of painting in [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai"). Later, he was trained in water painting by Rama Swami Naidu and rather reluctantly in [oil painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_painting "Oil painting") by British portraitist Theodore Jenson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-8)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg)

The studio used by Varma during his stay at the [Laxmi Vilas Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace "Laxmi Vilas Palace")

The British administrator, [Edgar Thurston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Thurston "Edgar Thurston") was significant in promoting the careers of Varma and his brother.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-9) Varma received widespread acclaim after he won an award for an exhibition of his paintings at Vienna in 1873. Varma's paintings were also sent to the [World's Columbian Exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Columbian_Exposition "World's Columbian Exposition") held in Chicago in 1893 and he was awarded three gold medals.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-10) He travelled throughout India in search of subjects. He often modelled Hindu [Goddesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddess "Goddess") on [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_India "South India") women, whom he considered beautiful. Ravi Varma is particularly noted for his paintings depicting episodes from the story of [Dushyanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushyanta "Dushyanta") and [Shakuntala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakuntala "Shakuntala"), and [Nala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nala "Nala") and [Damayanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damayanti "Damayanti"), from the [Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata"). Ravi Varma's representation of [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") characters has become a part of the Indian imagination of the epics. He is often criticized for being too showy and sentimental in his style but his work remains very popular in India. Many of his fabulous paintings are housed at [Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace,_Vadodara "Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-11)

## Raja Ravi Varma Press

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Raja Ravi Varma Press")]

_Mrs. Ramanadha Rao and son_

Apparently on the advice of the then Dewan (Prime Minister) of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"), [T. Madhava Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._Madhava_Rao "T. Madhava Rao"), Ravi Varma started a lithographic printing press in [Ghatkopar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghatkopar "Ghatkopar"), Mumbai in 1894 and later shifted it to Malavli near [Lonavala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonavala "Lonavala"), Maharashtra in 1899. The [oleographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleographs "Oleographs") produced by the press were mostly of Hindu gods and goddesses in scenes adapted mainly from the _[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_, the _[Ramayana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramayana "Ramayana")_ and the _[Puranas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puranas "Puranas")_. These oleographs were very popular and continued to be printed in thousands for many years, even after the 1906 death of Ravi Varma.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Ravi Varma press was the largest and most innovative press in India at that time. The press was managed by Varma's brother, Raja Varma, but under their management, it was a commercial failure. By 1899 the press was deeply in debt and in 1901, the press was sold to his printing technician from Germany, Fritz Schleicher. Schleicher continued to print Ravi Varma's prints but later employed other artists to create new designs. Schleicher also broadened the product of press to include commercial and advertisement labels. Under the management of Schleicher and his successors, the press continued successfully until a devastating fire destroyed the whole factory in 1972. Many of Ravi Varma's original lithographic prints were also lost in the fire.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-12)

## Honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honours")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma_1971_stamp_of_India.jpg)

Raja Ravi Varma on a 1971 stamp of India

In 1904, [Viceroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroy_of_India "Viceroy of India")[Lord Curzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Curzon "Lord Curzon"), on behalf of the British King Emperor, bestowed upon Varma the [Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaisar-i-Hind_Gold_Medal "Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal"). A college dedicated to [fine arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_art "Fine art") was also constituted in his honour at [Mavelikara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavelikara "Mavelikara"), [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). Raja Ravi Varma High at [Kilimanoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor "Kilimanoor") was named after him and there are many cultural organizations throughout India bearing his name. In 2013, the crater Varma on [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)") was named in his honor.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-13) Considering his vast contribution to [Indian art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_art "Indian art"), the Government of Kerala has instituted an award called [Raja Ravi Varma Puraskaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma_Puraskaram "Raja Ravi Varma Puraskaram"), which is awarded every year to people who show excellence in the field of art and culture.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-14)

*   On his 65th death anniversary, India Post issued a commemorative postal stamp depicting Ravi Varma and his famous painting 'Damayanti and Swan'

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Raja Ravi Varma is sometimes regarded as the first modern Indian artist due to his ability to reconcile Western aesthetics with Indian iconography. The Indian art historian and critic [Geeta Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Kapur "Geeta Kapur") wrote,

> Ravi Varma is the indisputable father figure of modern Indian art. Naive and ambitious at the same time, he opens up the debate for his later compatriots in the specific matter of defining individual genius through professional acumen, of testing modes of cultural adaptation with idiosyncratic effect, of attempting pictorial narration with its historic scope.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-15)

Similarly, Baroda School artist [Gulam Mohammed Sheikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulam_Mohammed_Sheikh "Gulam Mohammed Sheikh") also wrote about Ravi Varma as a modern artist. In his essay "Ravi Varma in Baroda", Sheikh asserted that Varma was a key figure in the establishment of Indian modern art, claiming that "the story of contemporary Indian art was never the same after Ravi Varma had entered it. He left his imprint on almost every aspect of it." Like Kapur, Sheikh praised Ravi Varma's integration of Indian and Western aesthetics and techniques, comparing him favorably to Indian modernist [Nandalal Bose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandalal_Bose "Nandalal Bose").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-16)

However, Ravi Varma's legacy is controversial. Fellow Baroda School artist and art historian [Ratan Parimoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratan_Parimoo "Ratan Parimoo") saw Ravi Varma in a less favorable light, derogatorily referring to him as [kitsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitsch "Kitsch") and claiming Varma's work was less spiritually authentic than folk art and tribal art. He argued that Ravi Varma was responsible for the "vulgarity" of popular art, comparing Varma's work to the lurid colors and sexuality of popular images in [calendar art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendar_art?action=edit&redlink=1 "Calendar art (page does not exist)") and films.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-18) Australian art critic [Christopher Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Allen_(critic) "Christopher Allen (critic)") made the same points in his review of the 2026 exhibition _The God of Small Things: Faith and Popular Culture_ at the [Queensland Art Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Art_Gallery "Queensland Art Gallery").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-19)

Despite his controversial legacy, Ravi Varma continues to be an important figure for modern and contemporary Indian artists. For example, modern artist [Nalini Malani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalini_Malani "Nalini Malani") recreated Ravi Varma's _[Galaxy of Musicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy\_of\_Musicians "Galaxy of Musicians")_ in her video installation _Unity in Diversity_ to interrogate Ravi Varma's idealistic nationalism.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-20) Similarly, contemporary artist [Pushpamala N.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushpamala_N. "Pushpamala N.") recreated several Ravi Varma paintings with herself as the subject to deconstruct Ravi Varma's idealized depictions of goddesses and Indian women.

Many organizations do programs in his memory and give awards in his name. A two days festival of The Maharaja Ranjitsinh Gaekwad Festival of Arts is annually organized, in his memory at the [Durbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durbar_(court) "Durbar (court)") Hall in [Laxmi Vilas Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace "Laxmi Vilas Palace"), [Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadodara "Vadodara"), [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-Sandesh2022-22) The Raja Ravi Varma Award for Excellence in the Field of Visual Arts is presented during this festival. [Jayant Parikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayant_Parikh "Jayant Parikh") was the first recipient.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-24)

## In popular culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Raja_Ravi_Varma&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

[J. Sasikumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Sasikumar "J. Sasikumar") made _Raja Ravi Varma_, an Indian documentary television film on the artist in 1997. It was produced by the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India")'s [Films Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Films_Division_of_India "Films Division of India").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-30)

_[Makaramanju](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makaramanju "Makaramanju")_ (English: _The Mist of Capricorn_) is a 2011 Indian [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam")-language romantic drama film by [Lenin Rajendran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenin_Rajendran "Lenin Rajendran") starring [Santosh Sivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh_Sivan "Santosh Sivan") as Varma, the film focuses on Varma's painting "Urvashi Pururavas".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-31) The 2014 Indian Hindi-language film, _[Rang Rasiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rang\_Rasiya "Rang Rasiya")_ (English title: _Colours of Passion_) explores Varma's inspiration behind his paintings with [Randeep Hooda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randeep_Hooda "Randeep Hooda") in the role of the painter.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja%20Ravi%20Varma#cite_note-hooda_paint-32)

**[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "w:Wikipedia")** is a free content, multilingual online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteers through a model of open collaboration, using a wiki-based editing system. Individual contributors, also called editors, are known as Wikipedians. Wikipedia is the largest and most-read reference work in history.

*   Who was Ravi Varma?  

Ravi Varma (1848–1906) was an Indian painter celebrated for blending Hindu mythological themes with European realism and naturalism. He was among the first Indian artists to use oil paints and master lithographic reproduction. Varma painted scenes from Hindu mythology and portraits of Indian and British figures in India. His notable works include _Shakuntala Writing a Love Letter to Dushyanta_ and _Shri Rama Vanquishing the Sea_.

Varma's work influenced Indian cinema and culture, with filmmaker Dadasaheb Phalke drawing inspiration from his religious iconography. Though some criticized his art as overly commercial and Westernized, interest in Varma's paintings has persisted. In 1904, he received the Kaiser-i-Hind medal and was popularly known as Raja Ravi Varma.

*   What is Ravi Varma famous for?  

Ravi Varma (1848–1906) was an Indian painter known for blending Hindu mythological subjects with European realism and naturalism. He was among the first Indian artists to use oil paints and master lithographic reproduction.

Varma painted portraits and scenes from the _Mahabharata_ and _Ramayana_ epics, capturing dramatic moments from Indian mythology using European techniques. His paintings, including _Harischandra in Distress_, _Jatayu Vadha_, and _Shri Rama Vanquishing the Sea_, realistically depict Hindu gods, goddesses, and epic characters. His idealized depictions of women, adorned in jewelry and saris, earned him gold medals at the World’s Columbian Exposition in Chicago in 1893.

Varma's work has influenced cinema, literature, and popular culture, with his religious iconography inspiring India’s first feature film, _Raja Harishchandra_ (1913).

*   How did Ravi Varma blend Indian and European art styles in his work?  

Ravi Varma, a celebrated Indian painter, masterfully combined Hindu mythological themes with European realist and naturalist painting styles. He employed European techniques of perspective and composition to create realistic oil paintings of Hindu gods, goddesses, and characters from Indian epics. Varma was one of the first Indian artists to use oil paints and master lithographic reproduction.

His work, while commercially successful and influential in Indian cinema and popular culture, faced criticism from artists who found it superficially Indian due to its imitation of Western styles. Despite the criticism, Varma's art, characterized by beauty and grace, has maintained enduring interest and influence.

*   How did Ravi Varma’s work influence later artists and popular culture in India?  

Ravi Varma's work significantly impacted later artists and popular culture in India. As one of the first Indian artists to use oil paints and master lithographic reproduction, his paintings blended Hindu mythological subjects with European realist styles.

Varma's religious iconography heavily influenced Dadasaheb Phalke, the father of Indian cinema, who borrowed from Varma's works in films such as _Raja Harishchandra_ (1913). Varma's artworks and visual motifs have since influenced cinema, literature, advertisements, music, and popular culture, including the _Amar Chitra Katha_ comic book series.

However, Varma faced criticism from later artists who viewed his work as superficially Indian due to its imitation of Western styles, which led to the formation of the Bengal School of Art. Despite the criticism, interest in Varma's art has remained constant, with his characteristic sense of beauty and grace evident in works like _The Maharashtrian Lady_, _Shakuntala_, and _The Milkmaid_.

**Ravi Varma** (born April 29, 1848, Kilimanoor Palace, near Trivandrum, Travancore [princely state](https://www.britannica.com/topic/princely-state-colonial-India), British India [now Thiruvananthapuram, [Kerala](https://www.britannica.com/place/Keralam), India]—died October 2, 1906, Kilimanoor Palace) was an Indian painter best known for uniting [Hindu](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Hinduism) mythological subject matter with European realist and naturalist painting styles. He was one of the first Indian artists to use oil paints and to master the art of [lithographic](https://www.britannica.com/technology/lithography) reproduction of his work. In addition to incidents in Hindu mythology, Varma painted many portraits of Indian and British people in India.

## Early education in art

Varma was born into an aristocratic family in the [erstwhile](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/erstwhile) princely state of [Travancore](https://www.britannica.com/place/Travancore) in southwestern [India](https://www.britannica.com/place/India). He showed an interest in art from an early age, drawing on the walls of the family mansion with [chalk](https://www.britannica.com/art/chalk-drawing) and [charcoal](https://www.britannica.com/art/charcoal-drawing). His uncle Raja Raja Varma, an artist in his own right, noticed his passion for art and gave him his first [rudimentary](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rudimentary) lessons in [painting](https://www.britannica.com/art/painting). When Varma was 13 or 14 years old, Ayilyam Thirunal, ruler of Travancore, became a patron of Varma’s early artistic career and allowed him to watch and learn from painters who practiced at the court. Varma was keen to learn [oil painting](https://www.britannica.com/art/oil-painting) but Ramaswamy Naidu, the only palace painter experienced in the medium at the time, refused to teach him, perhaps unwilling to give away his secrets to a potential rival. Arumugham Pillai, one of Naidu’s assistants, eventually taught Varma the basics of the technique in secret. Varma was later allowed to observe the oil painting of Theodore Jensen, a Danish-born British artist who came to the Travancore court in 1868, though Jensen also refused him formal training.

## Career as a professional artist

## Royal portraits

In 1870 Varma began his career as a professional painter—considered an inappropriate occupation for an [aristocrat](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/aristocrat) at the time—with a commissioned portrait of a family in Calicut (now [Kozhikode](https://www.britannica.com/place/Kozhikode)). Shortly afterward he painted a portrait of Thirunal and his wife, which led to his appointment as the palace artist at Trivandrum (now [Thiruvananthapuram](https://www.britannica.com/place/Thiruvananthapuram)). Varma won the Governor’s Gold Medal for the painting _Nair Lady Adorning Her Hair_ in 1873 and for _A Tamil Lady Playing the Sarabat_ the following year. These wins in India and another award at an [international exhibition](https://www.britannica.com/money/trade-show) in [Vienna](https://www.britannica.com/place/Vienna) made him a much-sought-after artist among both the Indian nobility and the Europeans in India, who commissioned him to paint their portraits.

## Mythology and religious themes

[![Image 11: Saraswati](https://cdn.britannica.com/42/74142-050-195AFA72/Hindu-deity-Sarasvati-painting-by-Rjaj-Ravi-Varma.jpg?w=300)](https://cdn.britannica.com/42/74142-050-195AFA72/Hindu-deity-Sarasvati-painting-by-Rjaj-Ravi-Varma.jpg)

[Saraswati](https://cdn.britannica.com/42/74142-050-195AFA72/Hindu-deity-Sarasvati-painting-by-Rjaj-Ravi-Varma.jpg)This Ravi Varma painting depicts Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of learning and the arts, in white, holding a veena and a manuscript.(more)

Alongside portraits, Varma increasingly painted subjects from Indian mythology. In 1876 his exhibition of _Shakuntala Writing a Love Letter to Dushyanta_, based on characters in the Indian epic [_Mahabharata_](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Mahabharata) and the subject of a [Sanskrit](https://www.britannica.com/art/Sanskrit-literature) play by poet [Kalidasa](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Kalidasa), was met with much acclaim. As his reputation grew, Varma was commissioned by royal families such as those of Baroda and Mysore to paint portraits and scenes from the _[Mahabharata](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Mahabharata)_ and another Indian epic, the _[Ramayana](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Ramayana-Indian-epic)_. His paintings, including _Harischandra in Distress_, _Jatayu Vadha_, and _Shri Rama Vanquishing the Sea_, captured dramatic moments from Indian mythology. He used European techniques of perspective and [composition](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/composition) to render realistic oil paintings of Hindu gods and goddesses as well as characters in the epics and the [Puranas](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Purana).

Idealized depictions of women are [pervasive](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pervasive) across Varma’s [oeuvre](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/oeuvre), both mythological and non-mythological. Often represented as sensuous and adorned in finely detailed [jewelry](https://www.britannica.com/art/jewelry) and [sari](https://www.britannica.com/topic/sari)s, these female forms are the predominant subjects of 10 paintings that Varma sent to the [World’s Columbian Exposition](https://www.britannica.com/event/Worlds-Columbian-Exposition) in [Chicago](https://www.britannica.com/place/Chicago) in 1893, where he was awarded two gold medals.

Did You Know?

In 1904 Varma was awarded the Kaiser-i-Hind, a medal to recognize distinguished public service in [British India](https://www.britannica.com/event/British-raj), which, until then, had been awarded exclusively to those engaged in trade and commerce. It was the inclusion of the title “Raja” in the [citation](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/citation) of this award that led to him being popularly called Raja Ravi Varma.

## Printing press

[![Image 12: Lakshmi](https://cdn.britannica.com/97/247597-050-87DC2FAB/Lakshmi-lithograph-Ravi-Varma-India-1894.jpg?w=300)](https://cdn.britannica.com/97/247597-050-87DC2FAB/Lakshmi-lithograph-Ravi-Varma-India-1894.jpg)

[Lakshmi](https://cdn.britannica.com/97/247597-050-87DC2FAB/Lakshmi-lithograph-Ravi-Varma-India-1894.jpg)The Hindu goddess Lakshmi, lithograph by Ravi Varma, c. 1894, one of a series of lithographs of Hindu gods by Varma.(more)

In 1894 Varma set up a lithographic [press](https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing-press) in order to mass-produce copies of his paintings as [oleographs](https://www.britannica.com/technology/oleograph) (prints on cloth to resemble oil paintings), enabling ordinary people to afford them. Because of financial difficulties, he sold the press and the copyrights for many of his paintings seven years later to a German printing technician, who began printing Varma’s artwork on a wide variety of products, including [calendars](https://www.britannica.com/science/calendar) and matchboxes. Because the press enabled his artworks to be widely distributed, Varma’s images of Hindu gods and goddesses, especially those of [Saraswati](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Saraswati) and [Lakshmi](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Lakshmi), have become some of the most recognizable and enduring representations of these figures in Indian households.

## Legacy and criticism

Did You Know?

[Dadasaheb Phalke](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Dadasaheb-Phalke), considered the father of Indian [cinema](https://www.britannica.com/art/film), [collaborated](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/collaborated) closely with Ravi Varma’s press. He would go on to make India’s first feature film, _Raja Harishchandra_ (1913), and several other mythological films that borrowed heavily from Varma’s religious iconography.

Despite the dismissal of Varma’s work by some as “calendar art” because of its commercialization, interest in his work has remained constant. In 1997, for example, _The Begum’s Bath_ sold for a record price for an Indian artist at the time. Works such as _The Maharashtrian Lady_, _Shakuntala_, _The Milkmaid_, _Expectation_, and _Pleasing_ exhibit Varma’s characteristic sense of beauty and grace. Varma’s artworks and visual motifs have influenced cinema, [literature](https://www.britannica.com/art/literature), [advertisements](https://www.britannica.com/money/advertisement), [music](https://www.britannica.com/art/music), and popular [culture](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/culture), including a popular [comic book](https://www.britannica.com/art/comic-book) series on Indian mythology published by Amar Chitra Katha.

Varma was criticized severely by later artists who saw the content of his work as only superficially Indian because, despite depicting mythological Indian themes, it imitated Western styles of painting. That view was instrumental in the formation of the [Bengal School of Art](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Bengal-School-of-Art) (or Bengal school), whose members explored ancient Indian artistic traditions with a modernist sensibility. Varma’s representations of Indian women have sometimes been panned for being stereotypical, exclusionary, and overly eroticized.

**Company school**, style of [miniature painting](https://www.britannica.com/art/miniature-painting) that developed in [India](https://www.britannica.com/place/India) in the second half of the 18th century in response to the tastes of the British serving with the [East India Company](https://www.britannica.com/topic/East-India-Company). The style first emerged in [Murshidabad](https://www.britannica.com/place/Murshidabad), [West Bengal](https://www.britannica.com/place/West-Bengal), and then spread to other centres of British trade: Benares ([Varanasi](https://www.britannica.com/place/Varanasi)), [Delhi](https://www.britannica.com/place/Delhi), [Lucknow](https://www.britannica.com/place/Lucknow), and [Patna](https://www.britannica.com/place/Patna).

The paintings were executed in watercolours on paper and on mica. Favourite subjects were scenes of Indian daily life, local rulers, and sets of festivals and ceremonies, in line with the “cult of the picturesque” then current in British artistic circles. Most successful were the studies of natural life, but the style was generally of a [hybrid](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/hybrid) and undistinguished quality.

Welcome!

Wikidata is a free and open knowledge base that can be read and edited by both humans and machines.

Wikidata acts as central storage for the **structured data** of its Wikimedia sister projects including Wikipedia, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary, Wikisource, and others.

Wikidata also provides support to many other sites and services beyond just Wikimedia projects! The content of Wikidata is [available under a free license](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), [exported using standard formats](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Database_download "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Database download"), and [can be interlinked to other open data sets](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Data_access "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Data access") on the linked data web.

Get involved

_For a complete starters’ guide, visit the **[community portal](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Community\_portal "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Community portal").**_
_**Learn about Wikidata**_

*   What is Wikidata? Read the **[Wikidata introduction](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Introduction "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Introduction")**.
*   Explore Wikidata by looking at a featured showcase item for author **[Douglas Adams (Q42)](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q42 "Q42")**.
*   Get started with Wikidata's **[SPARQL query service](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:SPARQL_query_service/Wikidata_Query_Help "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:SPARQL query service/Wikidata Query Help")**.

_**Contribute to Wikidata**_

*   Learn to edit Wikidata: follow the **[tutorials](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Tours "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Tours")**.
*   Work with other volunteers on a subject that interests you: **[join a WikiProject](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:WikiProjects "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:WikiProjects")**.
*   Individuals and organizations can also **[donate data](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Data_donation "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Data donation")**.

_**Meet the Wikidata community**_

*   Visit the **[community portal](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Community_portal "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Community portal")** or attend a **[Wikidata event](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Events "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Events")**.
*   Create a **[user account](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:CreateAccount "Special:CreateAccount")**.
*   Talk and ask questions on the **[Project chat](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Project_chat "Special:MyLanguage/Wikidata:Project chat")**, **[Telegram groups](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Telegram#Wikidata "meta:Special:MyLanguage/Telegram")**, or the **[live IRC chat](irc://irc.libera.chat/wikidata)**[connect](https://web.libera.chat/?channel=#wikidata).

News

*   The Wikidata [Query Service Days 2026](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Event:Query_Service_Days_2026 "Special:MyLanguage/Event:Query Service Days 2026") is coming soon! **October 17 to 23**. 
    *   This online event will focus on the migration of the Wikidata Query Service from Blazegraph to QLever, and supporting the Wikidata community, tool maintainers and data reusers with adapting their queries and tools to the new endpoint.
    *   🗓️ [Session program is out now](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Event:Query_Service_Days_2026#Sessions "Special:MyLanguage/Event:Query Service Days 2026"), and is designed to repeat sessions for different timezones, ensuring we reach as many Wikimedians as possible.
    *   🔗 [Register](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:RegisterForEvent/4448 "Special:RegisterForEvent/4448") for news, updates and most importantly, access links to the conferencing software.
    *   🗣️ Please share this event with anyone you know who makes use of SPARQL, the Wikidata Query Service or Wikidata lists, as there is a very high chance they will be affected!

*   2026-10-07: The Wikidata development team held the Q4 Wikidata+Wikibase office hour for 2026. They presented their work from the past quarter and discussed what's coming next. The official, non-commercial [sister site](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Main_Page#siteContainer)**of Wikipedia** for sightseeing, activities, cuisine and accommodation around the world.

Got a specific question? Ask it at the [travel forum](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Wikivoyage:Travel_forum "Wikivoyage:Travel forum").

### [Discover](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Discover "Discover")

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Sanjeong_Lake_%28%ED%8F%AC%EC%B2%9C_%EC%82%B0%EC%A0%95%ED%98%B8%EC%88%98%29_1%2C_December_2016.jpg/250px-Sanjeong_Lake_%28%ED%8F%AC%EC%B2%9C_%EC%82%B0%EC%A0%95%ED%98%B8%EC%88%98%29_1%2C_December_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikivoyage.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/File:Sanjeong_Lake_(%ED%8F%AC%EC%B2%9C_%EC%82%B0%EC%A0%95%ED%98%B8%EC%88%98)_1,_December_2016.jpg)

*   Surrounded by small mountains, **Sanjeong Lake** (_pictured_) outside [Pocheon](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Pocheon "Pocheon") is particularly popular during spring and fall when there is **night fog** on the lake.
*   **NSW's newest town**[Coleambally](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Coleambally "Coleambally") was officially opened in 1968 to serve as the administrative, commercial and social centre of the Coleambally Irrigation Area.
*   Founded by **French Huguenot** settlers who fled the Inquisition in Europe, [Franschhoek](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Franschhoek "Franschhoek") makes a serious attempt at being the **food and wine capital** of South Africa.

Wikipedia[e] is a free online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteer editors, known as Wikipedians, through open collaboration and the wiki software MediaWiki. Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, Wikipedia has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit organization funded mainly by donations from readers.[1] Wikipedia is the largest and most read reference work in history.[2][3]

Initially available only in English, Wikipedia has grown to over 300 languages and is one of the world's most visited websites as of 2026. The English Wikipedia, with over 7 million articles, remains the largest of the editions, which together comprise more than 68 million articles and attract more than 1.5 billion unique device visits and 13 million edits per month (about five edits per second on average) as of April 2024.[4] As of December 2025, over 25% of Wikipedia's traffic comes from the United States, while Japan accounts for nearly 7%, and the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia each represent around 5%.[5]

Wikipedia has been praised for its internal structure and culture, enabling the democratization of knowledge, and for its extensive coverage on various topics. The encyclopedia has also been criticized for systemic bias, such as a gender bias against women and a geographical bias against the Global South.[6][7] The reliability of Wikipedia was frequently criticized in the 2000s, but has received greater praise from the late 2010s onward.[2][8] Censorship of Wikipedia by national governments has ranged from censoring specific pages to the entire site, sometimes due to its criticism of the government, or for content considered blasphemous.[9][10] Wikipedia articles on breaking news are accessed as sources for up-to-date information by many.[11][12]

History
Wikipedia founders Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger both in 2026
Main article: History of Wikipedia
Nupedia
Main article: Nupedia

Various collaborative online encyclopedias were attempted before Wikipedia's launch, but with limited success.[13] Wikipedia began as a complementary project for Nupedia, a free online English-language encyclopedia project whose articles were written by experts and reviewed under a formal process.[14] It was founded on March 9, 2000, under the ownership of Bomis, a web portal company. Its main figures were Bomis CEO Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger, editor-in-chief for Nupedia and later Wikipedia.[15][16] Nupedia was initially licensed under its own Nupedia Open Content License. Before Wikipedia was founded, Nupedia switched to the GNU Free Documentation License at the urging of Richard Stallman.[17] Wales is often credited with defining the goal of making a publicly editable encyclopedia,[18] while Sanger is credited with the strategy of using a wiki to reach that goal.[19] On January 10, 2001, Sanger proposed on the Nupedia mailing list to create a wiki as a "feeder" project for Nupedia.[20]

Launch and growth

Wikipedia was launched on January 15, 2001 (sometimes referred to as "Wikipedia Day"),[21] as a single English language edition with the domain name www.wikipedia.com,[22] and was announced by Sanger on the Nupedia mailing list.[18] The name, proposed by Sanger to forestall any potential damage to the Nupedia name,[23] originated from a blend of the words wiki and encyclopedia.[24][25] Wales stated that the idea for Wikipedia was influenced by the spontaneous order ideas associated with Friedrich Hayek and the Austrian School of economics after being exposed to these ideas by the libertarian economist Mark Thornton.[26][27] In particular, Wales was influenced by Hayek's essay The Use of Knowledge in Society stating it was "central" to his thinking about "how to manage the Wikipedia project".[27] Its integral policy of "neutral point of view" arose within its first year.[28] Otherwise, there were initially relatively few rules, and it operated independently of Nupedia.[18] Bomis originally intended for it to be a for-profit business.[29]

The Wikipedia home page on December 20, 2001[f]

Wikipedia gained early contributors from Nupedia, Slashdot postings, and web search engine indexing. Language editions were created beginning in March 2001, with a total of 161 in use by the end of 2004.[30][31] Nupedia and Wikipedia coexisted until the former's servers were taken down permanently in 2003, and its text was incorporated into Wikipedia. The English Wikipedia passed the mark of 2 million articles on September 9, 2007, making it the largest encyclopedia ever assembled, surpassing the Yongle Encyclopedia made in China during the Ming dynasty in 1408, which had held the record for almost 600 years.[32]

Due to fears of commercial advertising and lack of control, users of the Spanish Wikipedia forked from Wikipedia to create Enciclopedia Libre in February 2002.[33] Wales then announced that Wikipedia would not display advertisements and changed Wikipedia's domain from wikipedia.com to wikipedia.org.[34][35]

After an early period of exponential growth,[36] the growth rate of the English Wikipedia in terms of the numbers of new articles and of editors appears to have peaked around early 2007.[37] The edition reached 3 million articles in August 2009. Around 1,800 articles were added daily to the encyclopedia in 2006; by 2013 that average was roughly 800.[38] A team at the Palo Alto Research Center attributed this slowing of growth to "increased coordination and overhead costs, exclusion of newcomers, and resistance to new edits".[36] Others suggested that the growth flattened naturally because articles that could be called "low-hanging fruit"—topics that clearly merit an article—had already been created and built up extensively.[39][40][41]

In November 2009, a researcher at the Rey Juan Carlos University in Madrid, Spain, found that the English Wikipedia had lost 49,000 editors during the first three months of 2009; in comparison, it lost only 4,900 editors during the same period in 2008.[42][43] The Wall Street Journal cited the array of rules applied to editing and disputes related to such content among the reasons for this trend.[44] Wales disputed these claims in 2009, denying the decline and questioning the study's methodology.[45] Two years later, in 2011, he acknowledged a slight decline, noting a decrease from "a little more than 36,000 writers" in June 2010 to 35,800 in June 2011. In the same interview, he also claimed the number of editors was "stable and sustainable".[46] A 2013 MIT Technology Review article, "The Decline of Wikipedia", questioned this claim, reporting that since 2007 Wikipedia had lost a third of its volunteer editors, and suggesting that those remaining had focused increasingly on minutiae.[47] In July 2012, The Atlantic reported that the number of administrators was also in decline.[48] In November 2013, New York magazine stated, "Wikipedia, the sixth-most-used website, is facing an internal crisis."[49] The number of active English Wikipedia editors has since remained steady after a long period of decline.[50][51]

On January 20, 2014, Subodh Varma reporting for The Economic Times indicated that not only had Wikipedia's growth stalled, it "had lost nearly ten percent of its page views last year. There was a decline of about 2 billion between December 2012 and December 2013. Its most popular versions are leading the slide: page-views of the English Wikipedia declined by twelve percent, those of the German version slid by 17 percent and the Japanese version lost 9 percent."[52] Varma added, "While Wikipedia's managers think that this could be due to errors in counting, other experts feel that Google's Knowledge Graphs project launched last year may be gobbling up Wikipedia users."[52] When contacted on this matter, Clay Shirky, associate professor at New York University and fellow at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society said that he suspected much of the page-view decline was due to Knowledge Graphs, stating, "If you can get your question answered from the search page, you don't need to click [any further]."[52] By the end of December 2016, Wikipedia was ranked the fifth most popular website globally.[53] As of January 2023, 55,791 English Wikipedia articles have been cited 92,300 times in scholarly journals,[54] from which cloud computing was the most cited page.[55]

Sister projects
Main article: Wikimedia project

Wikipedia has spawned several sister projects, which are also wikis run by the Wikimedia Foundation. These other Wikimedia projects include Wiktionary, a dictionary project launched in December 2002,[56] Wikiquote, a collection of quotations created a week after Wikimedia launched,[57] Wikibooks, a collection of collaboratively written free textbooks and annotated texts,[58] Wikimedia Commons, a site devoted to free-knowledge multimedia,[59] Wikinews, for collaborative journalism[60] (which was later shut down in 2026[61]), and Wikiversity, a project for the creation of free learning materials and the provision of online learning activities.[62] Another sister project of Wikipedia, Wikispecies, is a catalog of all species, but is not open for public editing.[63] In 2012, Wikivoyage, an editable travel guide,[64] and Wikidata, an editable knowledge base, launched.[65]
