Objectives

(1) T o study the present status of migration in study area, and,(2) T o study the causes and consequences of migration and to suggest measures to reduce the migration in the study area.

Database and Methodology

Over the years, migration from rural areas to urban areas has emerged as a major problem in Tehri district of Uttarakhand state. Therefore, in this research paper, an in-depth study of the causes and effects of migration in T ehri district has been done, so that measures can be taken to solve this problem. This research paper is complete ly based on secondary data. Secondary data has been obtaine d from Uttarakhand Government's Rural Development and Migration Commission report 2019-2020 and District Census Handbook 2011. After collection of data, the data has been analyzed through maps and diagrams. Data analysis has been done by Microsoft excel software and mapping by Arc GIS 10.4.1and Q-GIS 2.18 software. In the writing of this rese arch paper, help has been taken from Uttarakhand government reports, books and research papers.

Title: 2.3K views · 21 reactions | Kilimanoor, the birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma, stands today as a living chronicle of art, memory, and lineage. Within its sprawling courtyards and ageing corridors, time seems to have slowed, preserving echoes of an era when imagination and brush met royal patronage. In Wanderers Between Worlds, a film produced by the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation and directed by Vikas Urs, the camera journeys through the palace as it stands today - home still to the artist’s descendants, suspended between decay and devotion.

The weathered beams, the whisper of footsteps on the floors, and the soft light that filters through carved windows. Drawing from The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma, it reawakens moments that once defined the daily rhythm of India’s greatest painter and his brother.

By supporting and producing films like Wanderers Between Worlds, the Foundation reaffirms its role as a guardian of heritage, not merely conserving artworks and archives but transforming them into living experiences that bridge history, art, and cinema. 

Through its vision, spaces like Kilimanoor are like portals into the creative soul of a timeless legacy.

## 15 Things You Need To Know About Raja Ravi Varma

*   September 08, 2016
*   by Artisera Editorial

Bringing detail and realism to Indian imagery with a delicate interplay of light and shadows, Raja Ravi Varma is known for his stunning canvasses that have influenced generations of Indian artists.

![Image 92](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravi-Varma-Blog-New-Facebook-Size_grande.jpg?v=1473312021)

![Image 93](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravivarma1_large.png?v=1473312277)_(A photograph of Raja Ravi Varma taken in the 1890's)_

Though a protégé of royalty who was known for his portraits of Kings, Queens and Aristocrats, Raja Ravi Varma was also the first to make lithographs of his artworks affordable and easily available, bringing fine art to the masses.

![Image 94](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Maharaja_Sayaji_Rao_grande.jpg?v=1473312559)_(Portrait of Maharaja Sayaji Rao of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_

The first to use European realism and art techniques with Indian subjects, his portrayal of Indian Gods and mythological characters shaped Indian “calendar art”, and greatly influenced Indian literature and the film industry!

[![Image 95](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/11_Artisera_Fine-art_Lithographs_Ravi-varma-press_Laxmi_1_grande.jpg?v=1473312796)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An oleograph by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the Goddess, Laxmi; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)

**Here are 15 interesting facts about Raja Ravi Varma that you must know.**

1. Ravi Varma was born in 1848 in Kilimanoor, Kerala into a family of scholars, poets and artists. His mother's family followed the matrilineal system of lineage and succession. Therefore, Ravi Varma belonged to the family of his mother, and his children belonged to the family of their mother.

![Image 96](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Studiorrv_grande.jpg?v=1473313011)_(Birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma with his studio in the foreground)_

2. When Ravi Varma was a young boy, his uncle recognized his artistic talent, and sent him to the then ruling king, Ayilyam Thirunal, who helped him receive an education in arts, exposed him to western styles of painting, and had him trained by the palace painter.

![Image 97](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_ravivarma_painting_50_historic_meeting_grande.jpg?v=1473313083)_(Painting by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the 3rd Duke of Buckingham being greeted by Maharaja Ayilyam Thirunal and Visakham Thirunal of Travancore)_

3. At the age of 18, Varma married 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi of the royal house of Mavelikkara. The couple were blessed with two sons and three daughters. One of his daughters, Mahaprabha Amma, features in some of his most famous paintings.

![Image 98](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__There_Comes_Papa__1893_grande.jpg?v=1473313330)_(A painting by Ravi Varma of his daughter Mahaprabha Amma, with one of her sons)_

4. In 1904, Viceroy Lord Curzon, on behalf of the British Emperor, bestowed upon Varma, the Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. The citation for this award mentioned the title 'Raja' for the first time against his name. Varma then continued to use this title much to the consternation of the then Maharaja of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal.

![Image 99](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/IMG_2524_grande.JPG?v=1473313448)_(The Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. Image souce: british-medals.co.uk)_

5. The fame of Raja Ravi Varma reached to such great heights, that the small town of Kilimanoor, Varma’s birthplace, had to open a post office, as letters and requests for paintings came flooding in for him from various corners of the country!

![Image 100](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Galaxy_of_Musicians_grande.jpg?v=1473313597)_('Galaxy of Musicians', one of Raja Ravi Varma's most famous works)_

6. During his time, oil painting was a new medium, and it was only artist Ramaswamy Naicker of Madurai who had the knowledge of oil painting techniques. Seeing Raja Ravi Varma as a potential rival, Naicker refused to teach him the technique. It was Arumugham Pillai, Naicker's student, who taught Varma the nuances of oil painting, sneaking into the latter’s house at night, much against the wishes of his teacher.

![Image 101](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_2_grande.jpg?v=1473316850)_(Two of Ravi Varma's popular works: Left - Woman Holding a Fruit; Right - Scene from Kalidasa's 'The Recognition of Sakuntala')_

7. Raja Ravi Varma started a lithographic printing press in 1894, which was eventually sold to a printing technician from Germany. The oleographs produced by the press, mainly depicting gods, goddesses, and scenes from Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas, were very popular and continued to be printed in thousands, for many years.

![Image 102](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/varma06_grande.jpg?v=1473313850)_(Some of Varma's paintings along with the lithography stones used in the press, at the Raja Ravi Varma Archival Museum, Manipal. Image source:indiaheritagevillage.org)_

![Image 103](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Artisera_Raja_Ravi_Varma_Jatayu_Vadham_grande.jpg?v=1473325623)_(Ravi Varma's 'Jatayu Vadham', depicting a scene from the Ramayana)_

8. In the early 20 th century, women from Chettinad, a region in Tamil Nadu, began decorating Ravi Varma’s lithographs with zardozi embroidery and glitter work. These embellished prints included those from the Ravi Varma press and other presses, and can be dated from early to mid 20th century.

[![Image 104](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/13_Artisera_Fine-art_Oleograph_7395_1_1024x1024_grande.jpg?v=1473314821)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An embellished oleograph with zari and textile, depicting the 'Shiv Parivaar'; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)

9. Raja Ravi Varma’s brother, C. Raja Raja Varma was an accomplished landscape artist. Most information about the life of Raja Ravi Varma is through ‘_The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma_’, written by his brother, who was also Varma’s assistant and business manager.

![Image 105](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_1_12f12238-5113-4682-a116-b6cd5adb07b6_grande.jpg?v=1473317489)_(Left: Portrait of C. Raja Raja Varma; Right: The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma)_

10. Raja Ravi Varma was specially commissioned by the Maharaja of Vadodara to create portraits of the royal family and paintings based on Hindu mythology. A large collection of these is still displayed at the Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara.

![Image 106](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/562137_grande.jpg?v=1473315152)_(The Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara. Image Source: wall.alphacoders.com)_

![Image 107](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Chinmabai_grande.jpg?v=1473315229)_(Portrait of Maharani Chimnabai of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_

11. In 2013, a crater on Mercury was named ‘Varma’ in his honour!

12. Two of Ravi Varma’s granddaughters were adopted into the royal family of Travancore, and their descendants comprise the royal family, including the present titular Maharajah of Travancore, Rama Varma VII, who ascended the throne in 2013.

[![Image 108](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/7_Artisera_Fine-art_Oleograph_7444_1_2048x2048_grande.jpg?v=1473316185)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(Chitra Lekha, oleograph by Raja Ravi Varma; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)

13. Raja Ravi Varma’s paintings were the inspiration for India’s largest selling comic book series, the Amar Chitra Katha comics!

![Image 109](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/KGrHqRHJEEE_WUp8yGCBQM5v38GPg--60_1_grande.jpg?v=1473315660)_(A rare copy of Amar Chitra Katha's 'Malavika')_

14. In 2014, a film based on the life of Raja Ravi Varma was released, titled _Rang Rasiya (Colours of Passion)_, starring actors Randeep Hooda and Nandana Sen.

![Image 110](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/zooooot_24_large.jpg?v=1473315720)_(A promotional poster for the film 'Rang Rasiya')_

15. In 2008, a sari featuring a reproduction of 11 paintings by Raja Ravi Varma, entered the Guinness Book of World Records as the most expensive silk sari. The main highlight of the saree is Varma’s famous ‘_Galaxy of Musicians’_. Priced at Rs. 40 Lakhs, and weighing 8 kilos, it took 36 skilled craftsmen 12 months to hand-weave this ‘vivaah-patu’ sari!

![Image 111](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/most-expensive-saree_grande.jpg?v=1473315935)_(The Vivaah Patu saree, depicting Varma's Galaxy of Musicians)_

Suffering from diabetes, Raja Ravi Varma breathed his last in October 1906. His artistic lineage continued through his son Rama Varma, who went on to study at the renowned J.J School of Arts, Mumbai. Today, even 110 years after Raja Ravi Varma's death, there is no doubt about the profound legacy left behind by the great artist.

[![Image 112](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Oleograph_large.jpg?v=1585205393)](https://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)

##### A reknowned palace in Kerala, renowned as the birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma, showcasing traditional Kerala architecture, a preserved art studio, and a legacy of cultural and artistic significance.

Kilimanoor Palace, located in the Kilimanoor village of Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, is a historic and culturally significant landmark. This sprawling complex, with its traditional Kerala architecture, lush surroundings, and rich history, offers visitors a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. The palace is particularly renowned as the birthplace of the celebrated Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma, making it an essential destination for art lovers, history enthusiasts, and tourists.

**Historical Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace has a history that spans several centuries, dating back to the early 18th century. The palace was originally built by the royal family of Travancore as a residential and administrative center. Over the years, it has been the site of significant historical events and has hosted many distinguished guests, including British officials and Indian royalty. The most notable historical figure associated with Kilimanoor Palace is Raja Ravi Varma, one of India's greatest painters. Born in 1848, Ravi Varma is celebrated for his pioneering work in Indian art, blending traditional Indian themes with European techniques. The palace remains a symbol of his artistic legacy and continues to attract art aficionados from around the world.

**Architectural Features**

Kilimanoor Palace is an exemplar of traditional Kerala architecture, featuring wide verandahs, spacious courtyards, and long corridors. The palace's red-tiled roofs and brilliant white walls add to its picturesque charm. The architectural design incorporates local materials like wood and laterite stone, reflecting the indigenous construction techniques of the time.

**Raja Ravi Varma Studio**

The Chitrashala studio, designed by Raja Ravi Varma and built around 1875, is a significant part of Kilimanoor Palace. The studio boasts large glass windows that flood the space with natural light, creating an ideal environment for painting. It houses a dusty, aged easel and other tools used by Varma. The serene and inspiring surroundings include views of the flowering garden and paddy fields, which influenced Varma's works.

**Cultural and Artistic Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace is not only a historical site but also a cultural hub that celebrates the artistic heritage of Kerala. The palace's association with Raja Ravi Varma adds immense cultural value, as his works played a crucial role in shaping modern Indian art. Varma's paintings are renowned for their depictions of Hindu mythology, portraits of Indian women, and use of vibrant colors and intricate details. The palace preserves his memory with prints of his famous paintings, photographs, and personal artifacts. The Kilimanoor Palace Trust continues to uphold Varma's legacy by maintaining the palace and organizing events to celebrate his contributions to art. The palace regularly hosts art exhibitions, cultural programs, and workshops, promoting the arts and preserving the legacy of Raja Ravi Varma. Visitors can explore the museum dedicated to his works, attend lectures on his contributions to art, and participate in activities that highlight the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

**Accommodation**

There are several accommodation options available in and around Kilimanoor, ranging from budget lodgings to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer comfortable stays with modern amenities, providing a convenient base for exploring Kilimanoor Palace and the surrounding attractions.

**Visitor Information**

The best time to visit Kilimanoor Palace is year-round, as its indoor setting ensures that weather conditions do not impact the experience, making it ideal for sightseeing and exploring the palace at any time.

Hiring a local guide can enhance the visitor experience by providing detailed information about the historical and cultural significance of the palace. Guides can also offer insights into the life and works of Raja Ravi Varma and the architectural features of the complex.

Kilimanoor Palace, with its historical significance, architectural splendor, and cultural heritage, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are an art enthusiast, a history buff, or a curious traveler, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal legacy and artistic traditions of Kerala. A visit to Kilimanoor Palace is not only an educational journey but also an opportunity to connect with the timeless beauty and cultural richness of Kerala's past.

🎨 Raja Ravi Varma: The Man Who Made Art for Everyone 🖌️

You saw in the reel how Raja Ravi Varma (1848–1906) revolutionized Indian art. But here’s what you might not know! 👇

🔹 A Royal Prodigy 👑 Born into the aristocracy of Travancore, Varma’s artistic journey began under the guidance of his uncle, Raja Raja Varma. Recognizing his talent, his family arranged for him to train under palace artist Rama Swamy Naidu and later, Dutch painter Theodor Jenson—helping him master oil painting, a rarity in India at the time.

🔹 European Techniques, Indian Soul 🇮🇳✨ Varma was one of the first Indian artists to blend Western realism with traditional Indian themes. He used depth, shading, and perspective—European techniques—to breathe life into Indian mythology, history, and portraits.

🔹 The Bollywood Connection 🎬 His aesthetic—elegant saree drapes, expressive figures, and idealized Indian beauty—shaped the way Indian women were depicted in cinema and pop culture. 

🔹 A Lasting Legacy 🌟 Though critics debated his mix of styles, his impact is undeniable. His works remain iconic, inspiring everything from modern artists to fashion designers.

## Kilimanoor Palace

* * *

Kilimanoor Palace

*   [DESTINATIONS NEAR BY](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kilimanoor-palace-thiruvananthapuram/374/)
*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kilimanoor-palace-thiruvananthapuram/374/)
*   [ACCREDITED ADVENTURE TOUR OPERATORS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kilimanoor-palace-thiruvananthapuram/374/)
*   [TRAVEL INFO](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kilimanoor-palace-thiruvananthapuram/374/)
*   [OTHER HERITAGE CENTERS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kilimanoor-palace-thiruvananthapuram/374/)

* * *

##### A reknowned palace in Kerala, renowned as the birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma, showcasing traditional Kerala architecture, a preserved art studio, and a legacy of cultural and artistic significance.

Kilimanoor Palace, located in the Kilimanoor village of Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, is a historic and culturally significant landmark. This sprawling complex, with its traditional Kerala architecture, lush surroundings, and rich history, offers visitors a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. The palace is particularly renowned as the birthplace of the celebrated Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma, making it an essential destination for art lovers, history enthusiasts, and tourists.

**Historical Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace has a history that spans several centuries, dating back to the early 18th century. The palace was originally built by the royal family of Travancore as a residential and administrative center. Over the years, it has been the site of significant historical events and has hosted many distinguished guests, including British officials and Indian royalty. The most notable historical figure associated with Kilimanoor Palace is Raja Ravi Varma, one of India's greatest painters. Born in 1848, Ravi Varma is celebrated for his pioneering work in Indian art, blending traditional Indian themes with European techniques. The palace remains a symbol of his artistic legacy and continues to attract art aficionados from around the world.

**Architectural Features**

Kilimanoor Palace is an exemplar of traditional Kerala architecture, featuring wide verandahs, spacious courtyards, and long corridors. The palace's red-tiled roofs and brilliant white walls add to its picturesque charm. The architectural design incorporates local materials like wood and laterite stone, reflecting the indigenous construction techniques of the time.

**Raja Ravi Varma Studio**

The Chitrashala studio, designed by Raja Ravi Varma and built around 1875, is a significant part of Kilimanoor Palace. The studio boasts large glass windows that flood the space with natural light, creating an ideal environment for painting. It houses a dusty, aged easel and other tools used by Varma. The serene and inspiring surroundings include views of the flowering garden and paddy fields, which influenced Varma's works.

**Cultural and Artistic Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace is not only a historical site but also a cultural hub that celebrates the artistic heritage of Kerala. The palace's association with Raja Ravi Varma adds immense cultural value, as his works played a crucial role in shaping modern Indian art. Varma's paintings are renowned for their depictions of Hindu mythology, portraits of Indian women, and use of vibrant colors and intricate details. The palace preserves his memory with prints of his famous paintings, photographs, and personal artifacts. The Kilimanoor Palace Trust continues to uphold Varma's legacy by maintaining the palace and organizing events to celebrate his contributions to art. The palace regularly hosts art exhibitions, cultural programs, and workshops, promoting the arts and preserving the legacy of Raja Ravi Varma. Visitors can explore the museum dedicated to his works, attend lectures on his contributions to art, and participate in activities that highlight the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

**Accommodation**

There are several accommodation options available in and around Kilimanoor, ranging from budget lodgings to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer comfortable stays with modern amenities, providing a convenient base for exploring Kilimanoor Palace and the surrounding attractions.

**Visitor Information**

The best time to visit Kilimanoor Palace is year-round, as its indoor setting ensures that weather conditions do not impact the experience, making it ideal for sightseeing and exploring the palace at any time.

Hiring a local guide can enhance the visitor experience by providing detailed information about the historical and cultural significance of the palace. Guides can also offer insights into the life and works of Raja Ravi Varma and the architectural features of the complex.

Kilimanoor Palace, with its historical significance, architectural splendor, and cultural heritage, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are an art enthusiast, a history buff, or a curious traveler, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal legacy and artistic traditions of Kerala. A visit to Kilimanoor Palace is not only an educational journey but also an opportunity to connect with the timeless beauty and cultural richness of Kerala's past.

Title: Krishna Shukla on Instagram: "🎨 Raja Ravi Varma: The Man Who Made Art for Everyone 🖌️
You saw in the reel how Raja Ravi Varma (1848–1906) revolutionized Indian art. But here’s what you might not know! 👇
🔹 A Royal Prodigy 👑 Born into the aristocracy of Travancore, Varma’s artistic journey began under the guidance of his uncle, Raja Raja Varma. Recognizing his talent, his family arranged for him to train under palace artist Rama Swamy Naidu and later, Dutch painter Theodor Jenson—helping him master oil painting, a rarity in India at the time.
🔹 European Techniques, Indian Soul 🇮🇳✨ Varma was one of the first Indian artists to blend Western realism with traditional Indian themes. He used depth, shading, and perspective—European techniques—to breathe life into Indian mythology, history, and portraits.
🔹 The Bollywood Connection 🎬 His aesthetic—elegant saree drapes, expressive figures, and idealized Indian beauty—shaped the way Indian women were depicted in cinema and pop culture. 
🔹 A Lasting Legacy 🌟 Though critics debated his mix of styles, his impact is undeniable. His works remain iconic, inspiring everything from modern artists to fashion designers.

Title: 2.3K views · 21 reactions | Kilimanoor, the birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma, stands today as a living chronicle of art, memory, and lineage. Within its sprawling courtyards and ageing corridors, time seems to have slowed, preserving echoes of an era when imagination and brush met royal patronage. In Wanderers Between Worlds, a film produced by the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation and directed by Vikas Urs, the camera journeys through the palace as it stands today - home still to the artist’s descendants, suspended between decay and devotion.

The weathered beams, the whisper of footsteps on the floors, and the soft light that filters through carved windows. Drawing from The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma, it reawakens moments that once defined the daily rhythm of India’s greatest painter and his brother.

By supporting and producing films like Wanderers Between Worlds, the Foundation reaffirms its role as a guardian of heritage, not merely conserving artworks and archives but transforming them into living experiences that bridge history, art, and cinema. 

Through its vision, spaces like Kilimanoor are like portals into the creative soul of a timeless legacy.

##### A historic palace in Thiruvananthapuram, built during the Travancore era, now serves as a cultural venue with notable architecture and India's first digital garden.

Kanakakkunnu Palace, located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, is not only an architectural marvel but also a vibrant cultural hub. The palace, perched on a hillock, was believed to have been built during the 19th century under the reign of the erstwhile king of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal. Originally constructed to serve as a guest house, this red-bricked structure with white stone dressings is a fine example of Kerala-Gothic Victorian-era architecture.

The palace's design is both elegant and functional, featuring a dignified neoclassical entrance portico and a circular hall adorned with magnificent crystal chandeliers and exquisite pieces of royal furniture. The surrounding grounds are equally captivating, with meadows, groves, and flowering shrubs creating a serene atmosphere. The palace is also home to India's first digital garden, where visitors can scan QR codes to learn about the various plants, including their botanical names, species, nativity, and distribution.

Today, the palace serves as a popular venue for a multitude of cultural events, seminars, and programs. Its close proximity to other important tourist sites, such as the Napier Museum and Trivandrum Zoo, makes it an integral part of the city's daily life.

The palace grounds include two auditoriums—the Nishagandhi Auditorium, an open-air venue, and the Sooryakanthi Auditorium. The palace premises come alive during the all-India dance festival organized by the Department of Tourism, which runs from October to March. This festival attracts visitors from across the country who come to witness mesmerizing classical performances.

Kanakakkunnu Palace is also a popular meeting point for locals who enjoy its pleasant environment. In the evenings, the palace grounds buzz with activity as families and friends gather to unwind after a busy day.

With its unique blend of architectural beauty and cultural significance, Kanakakkunnu Palace remains a cherished landmark in Thiruvananthapuram, continuing to play a central role in the city's cultural and social life.

Title: 1.3K views · 17 reactions | Meet Jay Varma, a direct descendant in the unbroken lineage of Raja Ravi Varma, carrying forward a legacy of artistic brilliance that spans generations. As a Founding Trustee of the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation, Jay brings an innate eye for stylistic detail — not only in the works of the master himself, but across the entire Ravi Varma school.

Born into art, Jay Varma is a remarkable photographer, known especially for his breathtaking captures of birds in their natural habitat. What many don’t know is that he is also a superbly skilled pencil artist, with a mastery of detail and form. His artistic journey led him to The Studio Incamminati in Philadelphia, where he undertook rigorous training in oil painting. Today, he maintains a small, deliberate body of work — sought-after pieces that find their way into discerning private collections.

From reimagining mythological themes to revisiting subjects once immortalised by Raja Ravi Varma, from evocative portraits to quiet studies, Jay Varma’s art is both an homage to his heritage and a voice uniquely his own.

As the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation marks 10 years, we invite you to hear from our Founding Trustee, whose artistry and stewardship continue to shape the way the legacy is preserved, interpreted, and celebrated. | Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation

* * *

In Kerala, every destination is a canvas painted with breathtaking beauty and grace. Tranquil backwaters that meander through every nook and cranny of the land, sun kissed hill stations, picturesque beaches with azure waters and much more await you here. Whether you seek adventure, relaxation, or cultural immersion, Kerala entices with its diversity and warm hospitality.

[![Image 4: Attractions](link_2)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/attractions/ [link_3])

#### Attractions

A rare blend of culture, cuisine, and tranquility. From the mist-covered hills of Munnar to the tranquil waters of Alappuzha, every moment in God’s Own Country is magic waiting to be unravelled.

[Explore](link_3)

[![Image 5: Places of Interest](link_4)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/places-of-interest/ [link_5])

Step into Kerala's enchanting tapestry of lakes, rivers, and bustling streets and embrace Kerala's charm where every waterway and street corner tells a tale of timeless allure.

[Explore](link_5)

[![Image 6: Art & Culture](link_6)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/art-and-culture/ [link_7])

A land where ancient traditions blend seamlessly with contemporary creativity. Discover Kerala's artistic heritage that continues to inspire and enchant visitors from around the globe.

[Explore](link_7)

[![Image 7: Picnic Spots](link_8)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/picnic-spots/ [link_9])

#### Picnic Spots

For never-ending fun and frolic, and quality time that deepens bonds, saunter over to Kerala's scenic picnic spots set amidst lush greenery and serene landscapes.

[Explore](link_9)

[![Image 8: Regions](link_10)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/regions/ [link_11])

#### Regions

A gem in India's southwestern coast, Kerala unravels itself in diverse regions each with unique allure. Discover the land's vibrant culture, lush landscapes and warm hospitality across its varied landscapes and enchanting destinations.

[Explore](link_11)

[![Image 9: Spirituality](link_12)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/spirituality/ [link_13])

The ancient temples, serene ashrams, and revered pilgrim centres of Kerala beckon seekers. Take a break, embark on a journey that will fulfil you from within.

[Explore](link_13)

[![Image 10: Unique Destinations](link_14)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/unique/ [link_15])

Explore the hidden gems of Kerala with a journey through its unique destinations, offering a blend of natural beauty, cultural heritage, adventure, and immersive experiences.

[Explore](link_15)

[![Image 11: Unexplored Central Kerala Destinations](link_16)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/unexplored-central-kerala/ [link_17])

#### Unexplored Central Kerala Destinations

Unveil the hidden gems of Central Kerala, a pristine landscape where emerald forests blend seamlessly with rich cultural heritage and quiet backwaters. Perfect for seekers of solitude and adventure alike, this route offers deep cultural immersion and unforgettable, raw natural beauty.

[Explore](link_17)

[![Image 12: Unexplored Malabar Destinations](link_18)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/unexplored-malabar-experiences// [link_19])

#### Unexplored Malabar Destinations

Journey into the untouched heart of North Malabar, where secluded golden beaches meet the mystical rhythms of ancient Theyyam rituals. Escape to a land of pristine backwaters and secret hill sanctuaries, offering a rare glimpse into Kerala's rawest beauty and deepest cultural roots.

[Explore](link_19)

## Kanakakkunnu Palace

* * *

Kanakakkunnu Palace

*   [DESTINATIONS NEAR BY](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kanakakkunnu-palace-thiruvananthapuram/226/)
*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kanakakkunnu-palace-thiruvananthapuram/226/)
*   [ACCREDITED ADVENTURE TOUR OPERATORS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kanakakkunnu-palace-thiruvananthapuram/226/)
*   [TRAVEL INFO](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kanakakkunnu-palace-thiruvananthapuram/226/)
*   [OTHER HERITAGE CENTERS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kanakakkunnu-palace-thiruvananthapuram/226/)

* * *

##### A historic palace in Thiruvananthapuram, built during the Travancore era, now serves as a cultural venue with notable architecture and India's first digital garden.

Kanakakkunnu Palace, located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, is not only an architectural marvel but also a vibrant cultural hub. The palace, perched on a hillock, was believed to have been built during the 19th century under the reign of the erstwhile king of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal. Originally constructed to serve as a guest house, this red-bricked structure with white stone dressings is a fine example of Kerala-Gothic Victorian-era architecture.

The palace's design is both elegant and functional, featuring a dignified neoclassical entrance portico and a circular hall adorned with magnificent crystal chandeliers and exquisite pieces of royal furniture. The surrounding grounds are equally captivating, with meadows, groves, and flowering shrubs creating a serene atmosphere. The palace is also home to India's first digital garden, where visitors can scan QR codes to learn about the various plants, including their botanical names, species, nativity, and distribution.

Today, the palace serves as a popular venue for a multitude of cultural events, seminars, and programs. Its close proximity to other important tourist sites, such as the Napier Museum and Trivandrum Zoo, makes it an integral part of the city's daily life.

The palace grounds include two auditoriums—the Nishagandhi Auditorium, an open-air venue, and the Sooryakanthi Auditorium. The palace premises come alive during the all-India dance festival organized by the Department of Tourism, which runs from October to March. This festival attracts visitors from across the country who come to witness mesmerizing classical performances.

Kanakakkunnu Palace is also a popular meeting point for locals who enjoy its pleasant environment. In the evenings, the palace grounds buzz with activity as families and friends gather to unwind after a busy day.

With its unique blend of architectural beauty and cultural significance, Kanakakkunnu Palace remains a cherished landmark in Thiruvananthapuram, continuing to play a central role in the city's cultural and social life.

Title: 1.3K views · 17 reactions | Meet Jay Varma, a direct descendant in the unbroken lineage of Raja Ravi Varma, carrying forward a legacy of artistic brilliance that spans generations. As a Founding Trustee of the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation, Jay brings an innate eye for stylistic detail — not only in the works of the master himself, but across the entire Ravi Varma school.

Born into art, Jay Varma is a remarkable photographer, known especially for his breathtaking captures of birds in their natural habitat. What many don’t know is that he is also a superbly skilled pencil artist, with a mastery of detail and form. His artistic journey led him to The Studio Incamminati in Philadelphia, where he undertook rigorous training in oil painting. Today, he maintains a small, deliberate body of work — sought-after pieces that find their way into discerning private collections.

From reimagining mythological themes to revisiting subjects once immortalised by Raja Ravi Varma, from evocative portraits to quiet studies, Jay Varma’s art is both an homage to his heritage and a voice uniquely his own.

As the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation marks 10 years, we invite you to hear from our Founding Trustee, whose artistry and stewardship continue to shape the way the legacy is preserved, interpreted, and celebrated. | Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation

[![Image 1: Kerala Tourism](https://www.keralatourism.org/images/logo/logo.png)](https://www.keralatourism.org/ "Home")

![Image 2: Art and Culture](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Fart-and-culture-1714035798_bc042c097b157e068db8.webp&w=3840&q=75)

2.   [Destination](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/)-
3.   Art and Culture

## Art and Culture

*   [INSTITUTIONS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/art-and-culture/)
*   [HERITAGE CENTERS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/art-and-culture/)
*   [GALLERIES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/art-and-culture/)

* * *

[![Image 3: Institutions](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Finstitutions-1714481105_ff42beb3765c992e2b5b.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/institutions/)

#### Institutions

Bastions of the classical arts, heritage and legacy of the land, every institution is a salute to excellence, cultural preservation, and societal progress.

[Explore](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/institutions/ "Institutions")

[![Image 4: Heritage Centers](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Fheritage-centers-1714481124_85365c364f43762788c9.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/heritage-centers/)

#### Heritage Centers

These repositories of artefacts and history that span centuries of history, art, and tradition invite visitors to delve deep into the diverse and storied heritage of the land.

[Explore](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/heritage-centers/ "Heritage Centers")

[![Image 5: Galleries](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Fgallery-1714481137_e5e3f7eec37e576e3d7f.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/gallery/)

#### Galleries

Come explore sacred sanctuaries where creativity and cultural expression flourish. Spaces that not only celebrate artistic excellence but also reflect Kerala's commitment to nurturing creativity.

[Explore](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/gallery/ "Galleries")

[![Image 1: Kerala Tourism](https://www.keralatourism.org/images/logo/logo.png)](https://www.keralatourism.org/ "Home")

## Spirituality

*   [TEMPLES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/spirituality/)
*   [MOSQUES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/spirituality/)
*   [CHURCHES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/spirituality/)
*   [SYNAGOGUES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/spirituality/)

* * *

[![Image 3: Temples](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Ftemples-1720416143_f3cce289c484ef2ce683.webp&w=3840&q=75)](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/temples/)

#### Temples

Windows into the spiritual and cultural tapestry of the land. Rhythmic chants, fragrant incense, and ancient rituals await you in these unparalleled sanctuaries of devotion and faith.

[Explore](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/temples/ "Temples")

#### Mosques

Kerala's mosques stand as architectural and cultural marvels, blending Islamic tradition with regional aesthetics. From the grandeur of the Cheraman Juma Masjid, India's oldest mosque, to the intricate art work of the Beemapally Mosque, each site reflects the state's rich Islamic heritage and invites exploration into its spiritual and architectural beauty.

## Places of Interest

Our rich history is a source of pride for every Keralite. The cultural and artistic lessons that have been passed down are of utmost importance to us. It is our heritage and hence across the state we have centers built to honor and preserve these traditions. From the Stone Age carvings of Edakkal caves to Kalamandalam, a University for performing arts, the teachings of our elders still thrive in modern day Kerala. Their gifts to us shall never be forgotten and each new generation adds its own input to the same. Come visit these locations for an insight into the legacy of the state.

##### A historic site in Kerala, known for its gateway to Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple, royal palaces, and vibrant cultural heritage, including annual Navarathri celebrations.

East Fort in Thiruvananthapuram is a vibrant and historically significant area, renowned for being the gateway to the iconic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This bustling hub, filled with shops, commercial sites, and a steady stream of visitors, has witnessed the evolution of the city from the days of the Travancore Kingdom to the present day. Recognizing its historical importance, the State Government has declared East Fort a heritage site, preserving its cultural and architectural legacy.

As visitors approach East Fort, they are immediately struck by the imposing white gateway on the eastern side, which faces the famous Chalai Bazaar. This gateway, built in 1747 by King Marthanda Varma, is the most prominent of the fort's gates. Nearby, the Vettimurichakotta Gate is home to C.V.N. Kalari, a well-known school of Kalaripayattu, Kerala's ancient martial art form. Directly aligned with the East Fort gate stands the majestic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This seven-storied temple, built in the traditional Kerala and Dravidian architectural styles, is dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. The temple is not only a place of worship but also a marvel of architectural beauty, attracting visitors from around the world.

One of the unique features near the temple is the Methan Mani, a distinctive clock with a man's face and two goats on either side, which adds to the charm of the area. The East Fort also has other significant gates, including Nariadachankotta, Padinjarekotta, and Azheekotta, each with its own historical relevance.

Inside the fort, visitors can explore various structures associated with the erstwhile royal family, including numerous palaces and buildings that showcase a blend of traditional and Western architectural styles. The Ananthavilasam Palace, built in 1880 by King Vishakam Thirunal, is a prime example of Baroque and Rococo architecture. Another must-visit site is Kuthiramalika, also known as the Horse Palace, named for the intricately carved wooden horses that adorn its upper floors.

The area is also home to the Navarathri Mandapam, which hosts the annual Navarathri celebrations. This ten-day festival is renowned for its music festival, which attracts prominent artists and musicians from across the country, making it a key cultural event in Thiruvananthapuram.

East Fort and its surrounding heritage sites offer a fascinating glimpse into Kerala's rich history, culture, and architectural splendor, making it a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists.

## Kuthiramalika Palace

* * *

Kuthiramalika Palace

*   [DESTINATIONS NEAR BY](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)
*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)

* * *

##### Historic palace near Padmanabhaswamy Temple, showcasing Kerala architecture, rare artifacts, and Maharaja Swathi Thirunal’s legacy.

Kuthiramalika Palace, also known as Puthenmalika Palace, is a magnificent example of traditional Kerala architecture and a treasure trove of royal artifacts. Located near the renowned Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, this palace was built by Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the Maharaja of Travancore, in the 19th century. Kuthiramalika, meaning "Mansion of Horses," gets its name from the 122 wooden horses that adorn the exterior walls of the palace. This historical monument is a must-visit destination for those interested in Kerala's rich cultural heritage and royal history.

**Architectural Splendor**

Kuthiramalika Palace is a stunning example of traditional Kerala architecture, showcasing intricate woodwork, detailed carvings, and elegant design. The palace is constructed primarily of teakwood, rosewood, marble, and granite, reflecting the opulence and craftsmanship of the era.

The palace's name, Kuthiramalika, derives from the 122 carved wooden horses that decorate the eaves of the structure. These exquisite carvings are a testament to the skill and artistry of the craftsmen of that time. The palace features typical Kerala architectural elements such as sloping tiled roofs, overhanging eaves, and spacious courtyards. These design elements not only enhance the aesthetic appeal but also provide natural ventilation and protection from the monsoon rains.

The interiors of the palace are adorned with intricate wooden carvings and traditional motifs. The ceilings, beams, and pillars are meticulously carved with floral patterns, mythological figures, and scenes from Hindu epics, showcasing the richness of Kerala's artistic heritage. The palace comprises numerous halls and rooms, each with its unique design and purpose. The grand halls are used for royal ceremonies and gatherings, while the smaller rooms served as living quarters for the royal family.

**Royal Artifacts and Museum**Kuthiramalika Palace is not just an architectural marvel but also a repository of royal artifacts and historical treasures. The palace has been converted into a museum that houses a fascinating collection of items that offer insights into the royal life and culture of Travancore. The museum displays several thrones, including the famous ivory throne used by the Maharajas of Travancore. The intricately designed wooden and ivory furniture reflects the luxury and elegance of the royal court.

Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the builder of the palace, was not only a ruler but also a renowned musician and composer. The museum exhibits a collection of traditional musical instruments used by the Maharaja, including veenas, mridangams, and flutes. The walls of the palace are adorned with paintings and portraits of the Travancore royal family and notable personalities of the time. These artworks provide a glimpse into the history and lineage of the royal family. The museum features an array of antiques, including ancient manuscripts, ceremonial costumes, jewelry, weapons, and other artifacts that offer a deeper understanding of the cultural and historical heritage of Kerala.

**Cultural Significance and Events**

Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a historical monument but also a vibrant cultural center that hosts various events and programs:

**_Swathi Sangeethotsavam:_**This annual music festival, held in January, commemorates the birth anniversary of Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma. The festival attracts renowned classical musicians and performers from across India, who come to pay tribute to the musical legacy of the Maharaja. The palace courtyard serves as the venue for these performances, creating a magical atmosphere that resonates with the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

_**Heritage Tours:**_ Guided tours of the palace are available, offering visitors a detailed understanding of its history, architecture, and the royal artifacts on display. Knowledgeable guides provide insights into the life and times of the Travancore royal family, making the visit a truly enriching experience.

**Accessibility and Accommodation**

Kuthiramalika Palace is easily accessible by road, being located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram city. The nearest railway station is Thiruvananthapuram Central, and the nearest airport is Trivandrum International Airport, both of which are within a few kilometers of the palace.

There are several accommodation options available in Thiruvananthapuram, ranging from budget hotels to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer modern amenities and are conveniently located near the city's major attractions.

Visitor Information: The palace museum has an entry fee, with different rates for adults and children. It is advisable to check the latest timings and entry fees before planning your visit.

Kuthiramalika Palace, with its stunning architecture, rich history, and cultural significance, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are exploring the intricate carvings, admiring the royal artifacts, or attending a cultural event, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. A visit to Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a journey through history but also an opportunity to connect with the artistic and cultural essence of this beautiful region.

# Thiruvananthapuram Festivals 2025 | Vasantholsavam | Flower Festival | Light Displays | New Year Events | Kerala Tourism | Festivals 2024-2025

[![Image 1: Kerala Tourism](https://www.keralatourism.org/images/logo/logo.png)](https://www.keralatourism.org/ "Home")

![Image 2: Vasantholsavam](https://www.keralatourism.org/_next/image/?url=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fktadmin%2Fimg%2Fpages%2Flarge-desktop%2Fvasantholsavam-1733744890_201c6ab434afc9af7638.webp&w=3840&q=75)

1.   [Home](https://www.keralatourism.org/)-

3.   [Other Events](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/tourism-events/)-
4.   Vasantholsavam

## Vasantholsavam

* * *

Vasantholsavam

*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)
*   [OTHER OTHER EVENTS](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)
*   [OTHER FESTIVAL](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)

* * *

Promising a rare visual treat, the annual flower festival Vasantholsavam at Kanakakkunnu Palace grounds here from December 24 to January 4 will feature an amazing variety of flowering plants, making it the grandest flower show ever held in the state capital.

Vasantholsavam, along with the annual Light Festival, is organized by the State Tourism Department and the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) in collaboration with various government and private institutions, enlivening the Christmas and the New Year season.

A stunning range of over 35,000 pots of flowering plants will be showcased at the event, curated by Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanical Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI), Palode.Flowers have started reaching the city from different parts of the country.A Chrysanthemum festival, displaying a profusion of over 8,000 chrysanthemum flowers and plants, will be a salient feature of this edition of the festival.Also on display will be a wide variety of dahlias, marigolds, petunias, zinnias, daisies, anthuriums, lilies, and tulips, besides a range of locally grown flowers.Several competitions have also been planned as part of the festival.

Government institutions including Museum and Zoo, State Legislature Secretariat, Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Government Agricultural College Vellayani, Tropical Botanical Garden, and Ayurveda Research Centre will be participating in competitions.

The visually fascinating event will be a double delight for visitors with the Light Festival illuminating the city's streets and heritage structures during the Christmas and New Year season.

The flower festival will have competitions in around 70 categories including those relating to exhibition of flower plants, ornamental plants, orchids, anthurium, cactus and adenium.

Government and private institutions, nurseries and individuals can take part in the competitions. There will be separate first, second and third prize winners, besides overall champions in each category.

An expo of flower decoration as well as a competition in this category will also be held for adults and students. Visitors can also buy flowers and plants from the stalls put up by various nurseries. Entry ticket for adults is Rs. 50, while for children it is Rs. 30.

## Disclaimer

In Kerala, festival dates are decided in accordance with the Malayalam calendar and the local traditions and customs. We have calculated the festival dates based on these. But there can be changes in the dates according the customs and rituals associated with each place of worship. As such, these should be considered only as approximate dates and have to be confirmed with the local authorities.

About Us

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation is a not-for-profit institution that works to preserve and promote the artistic legacy of one of India’s greatest artists. Started by his great, great granddaughter Bharani Thirunal Rukmini Bayi Tampuran in 2015, the Foundation’s activities are ably guided and managed by an expert panel of external and internal advisors, in the field of art, history, conservation and industry.

The Foundation is the only institution in the world that works in the space of research, documentation, authentication and education with regard to Ravi Varma and his art works. The Foundation works with public and private museums, collectors and any collections that house or own works by this incredible artist.

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Significance of the logo

The name Varma is derived from the original Sanskrit word “Varman” which means “armour” or “protection” or “shield”. The name Varma came to be used to refer to a Chief or Protector of an exclusive clan. The members of this clan were the Kshatriyas. The ancient source from where the people who belonged to this clan is believed to have originated somewhere in Central Asia. A King from Southern India, notably present day Kerala, by the name of Varma also finds mention in the Mahabharata war.

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation, with its new logo, embraces Varma or the Shield in an appropriate and distinct manner. The intent behind the Foundation’s logo is in keeping with our endeavour to protect his artistic legacy and the creative direction that Ravi Varma showed during his lifetime.

The presence of the Trident in our logo is significant in that it is an invaluable accessory to the protective armour or shield.

While we have embraced a new logo which is bright, bold and beautiful, our principles at the Foundation remain unchanged and firmly entrenched in Ravi Varma’s ideals. Our endeavour is to preserve and promote the rich legacy of one of India’s greatest artists.

- Rukmini Varma

_Chairperson, Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation_

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Our Objectives

Briefly, these are to:

1. Increase awareness of his work through lecture series, exhibitions, short films and books

2. Promote his legacy and document his influences on jewellery, textiles and on other artists, through exhibits and talks

3. Provide valid authentication for his original works created in oil

## Ab out Raja Ravi Varma

![Image 21](https://l.facebook.com/images/photos/about-img1.jpg)

The life and works of one of India's most prolific artists.

Raja Ravi Varma was a painter par excellence whose works not only put India on the map but also placed him on the pedestal with other great artists. Born 29 April, 1848 at Kilimanoor in the erstwhile State of Travancore, Ravi Varma’s paintings of the Royals, illustrious personalities and contemporary figures were widely sought-after and greatly admired.

An eye for detail, splendid use of colours and rich texture gave his paintings a classy, exquisite look, the reason why his works are priceless even to this day.

His realistic portrayals and interpretations of religious and mythological figures that adorn the households today, captivated and fascinated the country as well as an international audience.

Ravi Varma’s works transcended painting; he was also a poet, scholar and a visionary far beyond his times. His work also helped focus attention on his talented peers and paved the way for a succession of artistes.

Ravi Varma’s intention was to take art to the common man and not to limit it just to a privileged few. By establishing a press to make reproductions of his works, Ravi Varma ensured a strong foundation of admiration and respect from all.

Passing away on 2nd October 1906 at the age of 58, Ravi Varma’s legacy continues to live and thrive through his works and the Foundation.

#### His Influence

Over the years many of us have forgotten how Raja Ravi Varma has influenced our lives in subtle, yet defining ways. His visual images of gods and goddesses which attained celestial reverence has impacted almost all walks of life. These can be related to his influence on Indian comic books, temple architecture, jewellery, textiles and ceramics to name a few.

## Ev ents

![Image 22: Ram Sagar darp haran - A S Desai](https://l.facebook.com/images/portfolio/sri-rama-vanquishing-the-sea.jpg)

A brief calendar of events & exhibitions

Since inception in 2015, the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation has successfully conducted and executed several exhibitions, talks, panel discussions and even made a short film on Raja Ravi Varma's birth place, in its effort to preserve his legacy - both artistic and otherwise.

Some of our most popular events have been:

*   _**Foundation’s Season Five -**_ The fifth year of the Foundation will go down as one of the most memorable. Having earmarked five speakers for what has been our Season Five, the Foundation enlisted the services of five speakers, diverse, yet distinct in their field, to talk about Ravi Varma and his art.

The RRVHF brought on board noted Oxford-based Prof. Partha Mitter, art expert and Yale University lecturer Patrick Connors, noted historian and conservator Rupika Chawla. While the three of them are distinguished in their respective fields, the Foundation, in keeping with the diverse tune, roped in Dinesh Vazirani, CEO and Co-Founder of SaffronArt, one of the top international auction houses. Vazirani’s interactive session was primarily to give his insight on the Art of Investment and to decode the myths surrounding auction houses and its processes.

As the finale to Season Five, the Foundation organized a talk by Deepanjana Pal, journalist and author of The Painter: A life of Raja Ravi Varma. Her perspective on the master artist and his works are different, yet relevant and it gelled well with our theme of bringing in five varied speakers to disseminate their knowledge on Ravi Varma and his art.

All the talks have been uploaded on YouTube and those desirous of watching the talk again may kindly click on the YouTube icon or [here](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCke9w2FMmyc8FZJymov5Q5A) and watch the desired event in full.

*   _**Ravi Varma & His Contemporaries -**_ Historian and conservation specialist Rupika Chawla was in conversation with author Manu S Pillai on the influence of the great master on a generation of contemporary artists like Sekhara Warrier, Mukundan Tampi, Neelakanta Pillai and others. The Foundational also worked with a group of private collectors displaying 11 original oil paintings for the day at the Kerala Museum, Kochi.
*   _**Raja Ravi Varma: His Mythological Perspectives -**_ Devadutt Pattanaik kept the audience engrossed, dwelling on the huge role that Ravi Varma played in bringing the gods and goddesses and mythological characters closer to the common man during his lifetime, by way of his art. Pattanaik explained the mythological essence in some of Ravi Varma’s works like Dhruva Narayan, Ambika, Shankar to name a few.

The chronological detailed listing of the events can be found in the link below:

[Foundation Events](https://l.facebook.com/events.html)

These events, all planned and curated by the Foundation, shed light on the artist's impact on mythology, music, jewellery and textiles among others.

# Muse — Your Personal AI Agent

Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://muse.ai/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://muse.ai/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://muse.ai/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://muse.ai/#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

![Image 8: The Muse app icon](https://muse.ai/images/landing/placeholders/sizzle.png)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 10: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://muse.ai/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 12: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://muse.ai/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://muse.ai/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 14: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://muse.ai/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://muse.ai/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 16: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://muse.ai/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 18: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 19: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://muse.ai/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 20: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://muse.ai/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://muse.ai/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

Log in

## East Fort and the Heritage Tour

* * *

East Fort and the Heritage Tour

*   [DESTINATIONS NEAR BY](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/east-fort-thiruvananthapuram/361/)
*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/east-fort-thiruvananthapuram/361/)
*   [ACCREDITED ADVENTURE TOUR OPERATORS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/east-fort-thiruvananthapuram/361/)
*   [TRAVEL INFO](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/east-fort-thiruvananthapuram/361/)
*   [OTHER HERITAGE CENTERS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/east-fort-thiruvananthapuram/361/)

* * *

##### A historic site in Kerala, known for its gateway to Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple, royal palaces, and vibrant cultural heritage, including annual Navarathri celebrations.

East Fort in Thiruvananthapuram is a vibrant and historically significant area, renowned for being the gateway to the iconic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This bustling hub, filled with shops, commercial sites, and a steady stream of visitors, has witnessed the evolution of the city from the days of the Travancore Kingdom to the present day. Recognizing its historical importance, the State Government has declared East Fort a heritage site, preserving its cultural and architectural legacy.

As visitors approach East Fort, they are immediately struck by the imposing white gateway on the eastern side, which faces the famous Chalai Bazaar. This gateway, built in 1747 by King Marthanda Varma, is the most prominent of the fort's gates. Nearby, the Vettimurichakotta Gate is home to C.V.N. Kalari, a well-known school of Kalaripayattu, Kerala's ancient martial art form. Directly aligned with the East Fort gate stands the majestic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This seven-storied temple, built in the traditional Kerala and Dravidian architectural styles, is dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. The temple is not only a place of worship but also a marvel of architectural beauty, attracting visitors from around the world.

One of the unique features near the temple is the Methan Mani, a distinctive clock with a man's face and two goats on either side, which adds to the charm of the area. The East Fort also has other significant gates, including Nariadachankotta, Padinjarekotta, and Azheekotta, each with its own historical relevance.

Inside the fort, visitors can explore various structures associated with the erstwhile royal family, including numerous palaces and buildings that showcase a blend of traditional and Western architectural styles. The Ananthavilasam Palace, built in 1880 by King Vishakam Thirunal, is a prime example of Baroque and Rococo architecture. Another must-visit site is Kuthiramalika, also known as the Horse Palace, named for the intricately carved wooden horses that adorn its upper floors.

The area is also home to the Navarathri Mandapam, which hosts the annual Navarathri celebrations. This ten-day festival is renowned for its music festival, which attracts prominent artists and musicians from across the country, making it a key cultural event in Thiruvananthapuram.

East Fort and its surrounding heritage sites offer a fascinating glimpse into Kerala's rich history, culture, and architectural splendor, making it a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists.

## Kuthiramalika Palace

* * *

Kuthiramalika Palace

*   [DESTINATIONS NEAR BY](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)
*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)

*   [TRAVEL INFO](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)
*   [OTHER HERITAGE CENTERS](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/kuthiramalika-palace-east-fort/58/)

* * *

##### Historic palace near Padmanabhaswamy Temple, showcasing Kerala architecture, rare artifacts, and Maharaja Swathi Thirunal’s legacy.

Kuthiramalika Palace, also known as Puthenmalika Palace, is a magnificent example of traditional Kerala architecture and a treasure trove of royal artifacts. Located near the renowned Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, this palace was built by Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the Maharaja of Travancore, in the 19th century. Kuthiramalika, meaning "Mansion of Horses," gets its name from the 122 wooden horses that adorn the exterior walls of the palace. This historical monument is a must-visit destination for those interested in Kerala's rich cultural heritage and royal history.

**Architectural Splendor**

Kuthiramalika Palace is a stunning example of traditional Kerala architecture, showcasing intricate woodwork, detailed carvings, and elegant design. The palace is constructed primarily of teakwood, rosewood, marble, and granite, reflecting the opulence and craftsmanship of the era.

The palace's name, Kuthiramalika, derives from the 122 carved wooden horses that decorate the eaves of the structure. These exquisite carvings are a testament to the skill and artistry of the craftsmen of that time. The palace features typical Kerala architectural elements such as sloping tiled roofs, overhanging eaves, and spacious courtyards. These design elements not only enhance the aesthetic appeal but also provide natural ventilation and protection from the monsoon rains.

The interiors of the palace are adorned with intricate wooden carvings and traditional motifs. The ceilings, beams, and pillars are meticulously carved with floral patterns, mythological figures, and scenes from Hindu epics, showcasing the richness of Kerala's artistic heritage. The palace comprises numerous halls and rooms, each with its unique design and purpose. The grand halls are used for royal ceremonies and gatherings, while the smaller rooms served as living quarters for the royal family.

**Royal Artifacts and Museum**Kuthiramalika Palace is not just an architectural marvel but also a repository of royal artifacts and historical treasures. The palace has been converted into a museum that houses a fascinating collection of items that offer insights into the royal life and culture of Travancore. The museum displays several thrones, including the famous ivory throne used by the Maharajas of Travancore. The intricately designed wooden and ivory furniture reflects the luxury and elegance of the royal court.

Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the builder of the palace, was not only a ruler but also a renowned musician and composer. The museum exhibits a collection of traditional musical instruments used by the Maharaja, including veenas, mridangams, and flutes. The walls of the palace are adorned with paintings and portraits of the Travancore royal family and notable personalities of the time. These artworks provide a glimpse into the history and lineage of the royal family. The museum features an array of antiques, including ancient manuscripts, ceremonial costumes, jewelry, weapons, and other artifacts that offer a deeper understanding of the cultural and historical heritage of Kerala.

**Cultural Significance and Events**

Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a historical monument but also a vibrant cultural center that hosts various events and programs:

**_Swathi Sangeethotsavam:_**This annual music festival, held in January, commemorates the birth anniversary of Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma. The festival attracts renowned classical musicians and performers from across India, who come to pay tribute to the musical legacy of the Maharaja. The palace courtyard serves as the venue for these performances, creating a magical atmosphere that resonates with the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

_**Heritage Tours:**_ Guided tours of the palace are available, offering visitors a detailed understanding of its history, architecture, and the royal artifacts on display. Knowledgeable guides provide insights into the life and times of the Travancore royal family, making the visit a truly enriching experience.

**Accessibility and Accommodation**

Kuthiramalika Palace is easily accessible by road, being located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram city. The nearest railway station is Thiruvananthapuram Central, and the nearest airport is Trivandrum International Airport, both of which are within a few kilometers of the palace.

There are several accommodation options available in Thiruvananthapuram, ranging from budget hotels to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer modern amenities and are conveniently located near the city's major attractions.

Visitor Information: The palace museum has an entry fee, with different rates for adults and children. It is advisable to check the latest timings and entry fees before planning your visit.

Kuthiramalika Palace, with its stunning architecture, rich history, and cultural significance, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are exploring the intricate carvings, admiring the royal artifacts, or attending a cultural event, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. A visit to Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a journey through history but also an opportunity to connect with the artistic and cultural essence of this beautiful region.

## Vasantholsavam

* * *

Vasantholsavam

*   [HOSPITALITY SERVICES](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)
*   [OTHER OTHER EVENTS](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)
*   [OTHER FESTIVAL](https://www.keralatourism.org/event/vasantholsavam-2023/581/)

* * *

Promising a rare visual treat, the annual flower festival Vasantholsavam at Kanakakkunnu Palace grounds here from December 24 to January 4 will feature an amazing variety of flowering plants, making it the grandest flower show ever held in the state capital.

Vasantholsavam, along with the annual Light Festival, is organized by the State Tourism Department and the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) in collaboration with various government and private institutions, enlivening the Christmas and the New Year season.

A stunning range of over 35,000 pots of flowering plants will be showcased at the event, curated by Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanical Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI), Palode.Flowers have started reaching the city from different parts of the country.A Chrysanthemum festival, displaying a profusion of over 8,000 chrysanthemum flowers and plants, will be a salient feature of this edition of the festival.Also on display will be a wide variety of dahlias, marigolds, petunias, zinnias, daisies, anthuriums, lilies, and tulips, besides a range of locally grown flowers.Several competitions have also been planned as part of the festival.

Government institutions including Museum and Zoo, State Legislature Secretariat, Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), Government Agricultural College Vellayani, Tropical Botanical Garden, and Ayurveda Research Centre will be participating in competitions.

The visually fascinating event will be a double delight for visitors with the Light Festival illuminating the city's streets and heritage structures during the Christmas and New Year season.

The flower festival will have competitions in around 70 categories including those relating to exhibition of flower plants, ornamental plants, orchids, anthurium, cactus and adenium.

Government and private institutions, nurseries and individuals can take part in the competitions. There will be separate first, second and third prize winners, besides overall champions in each category.

An expo of flower decoration as well as a competition in this category will also be held for adults and students. Visitors can also buy flowers and plants from the stalls put up by various nurseries. Entry ticket for adults is Rs. 50, while for children it is Rs. 30.

## Disclaimer

In Kerala, festival dates are decided in accordance with the Malayalam calendar and the local traditions and customs. We have calculated the festival dates based on these. But there can be changes in the dates according the customs and rituals associated with each place of worship. As such, these should be considered only as approximate dates and have to be confirmed with the local authorities.
