# Muse — Your Personal AI Agent

Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://muse.ai/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://muse.ai/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://muse.ai/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://muse.ai/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://muse.ai/#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

![Image 8: The Muse app icon](https://muse.ai/images/landing/placeholders/sizzle.png)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 10: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://muse.ai/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 12: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://muse.ai/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://muse.ai/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 14: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://muse.ai/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://muse.ai/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 16: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://muse.ai/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 18: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://muse.ai/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 19: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://muse.ai/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 20: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://muse.ai/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://muse.ai/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

Log in

## Places of Interest

Our rich history is a source of pride for every Keralite. The cultural and artistic lessons that have been passed down are of utmost importance to us. It is our heritage and hence across the state we have centers built to honor and preserve these traditions. From the Stone Age carvings of Edakkal caves to Kalamandalam, a University for performing arts, the teachings of our elders still thrive in modern day Kerala. Their gifts to us shall never be forgotten and each new generation adds its own input to the same. Come visit these locations for an insight into the legacy of the state.

![Image 6: kilimanoor palace](https://l.facebook.com/images/photos/insignia.png)

About Us

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation is a not-for-profit institution that works to preserve and promote the artistic legacy of one of India’s greatest artists. Started by his great, great granddaughter Bharani Thirunal Rukmini Bayi Tampuran in 2015, the Foundation’s activities are ably guided and managed by an expert panel of external and internal advisors, in the field of art, history, conservation and industry.

The Foundation is the only institution in the world that works in the space of research, documentation, authentication and education with regard to Ravi Varma and his art works. The Foundation works with public and private museums, collectors and any collections that house or own works by this incredible artist.

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Significance of the logo

The name Varma is derived from the original Sanskrit word “Varman” which means “armour” or “protection” or “shield”. The name Varma came to be used to refer to a Chief or Protector of an exclusive clan. The members of this clan were the Kshatriyas. The ancient source from where the people who belonged to this clan is believed to have originated somewhere in Central Asia. A King from Southern India, notably present day Kerala, by the name of Varma also finds mention in the Mahabharata war.

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation, with its new logo, embraces Varma or the Shield in an appropriate and distinct manner. The intent behind the Foundation’s logo is in keeping with our endeavour to protect his artistic legacy and the creative direction that Ravi Varma showed during his lifetime.

The presence of the Trident in our logo is significant in that it is an invaluable accessory to the protective armour or shield.

While we have embraced a new logo which is bright, bold and beautiful, our principles at the Foundation remain unchanged and firmly entrenched in Ravi Varma’s ideals. Our endeavour is to preserve and promote the rich legacy of one of India’s greatest artists.

- Rukmini Varma

_Chairperson, Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation_

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Our Objectives

Briefly, these are to:

1. Increase awareness of his work through lecture series, exhibitions, short films and books

2. Promote his legacy and document his influences on jewellery, textiles and on other artists, through exhibits and talks

3. Provide valid authentication for his original works created in oil

## Ab out Raja Ravi Varma

![Image 21](https://l.facebook.com/images/photos/about-img1.jpg)

The life and works of one of India's most prolific artists.

Raja Ravi Varma was a painter par excellence whose works not only put India on the map but also placed him on the pedestal with other great artists. Born 29 April, 1848 at Kilimanoor in the erstwhile State of Travancore, Ravi Varma’s paintings of the Royals, illustrious personalities and contemporary figures were widely sought-after and greatly admired.

An eye for detail, splendid use of colours and rich texture gave his paintings a classy, exquisite look, the reason why his works are priceless even to this day.

His realistic portrayals and interpretations of religious and mythological figures that adorn the households today, captivated and fascinated the country as well as an international audience.

Ravi Varma’s works transcended painting; he was also a poet, scholar and a visionary far beyond his times. His work also helped focus attention on his talented peers and paved the way for a succession of artistes.

Ravi Varma’s intention was to take art to the common man and not to limit it just to a privileged few. By establishing a press to make reproductions of his works, Ravi Varma ensured a strong foundation of admiration and respect from all.

Passing away on 2nd October 1906 at the age of 58, Ravi Varma’s legacy continues to live and thrive through his works and the Foundation.

#### His Influence

Over the years many of us have forgotten how Raja Ravi Varma has influenced our lives in subtle, yet defining ways. His visual images of gods and goddesses which attained celestial reverence has impacted almost all walks of life. These can be related to his influence on Indian comic books, temple architecture, jewellery, textiles and ceramics to name a few.

## Wo rks

Raja Ravi Varma's works are catalogued here as Paintings (Oils), Portraits (Oils) and Works from the Raja Ravi Varma Press and others across India. His vision helped forge a new identity and stature for Indian art by fusing Indian tradition and classical European technique. The list is exhaustive and hence we showcase a few of his significant works.

##### Historic palace near Padmanabhaswamy Temple, showcasing Kerala architecture, rare artifacts, and Maharaja Swathi Thirunal’s legacy.

Kuthiramalika Palace, also known as Puthenmalika Palace, is a magnificent example of traditional Kerala architecture and a treasure trove of royal artifacts. Located near the renowned Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, this palace was built by Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the Maharaja of Travancore, in the 19th century. Kuthiramalika, meaning "Mansion of Horses," gets its name from the 122 wooden horses that adorn the exterior walls of the palace. This historical monument is a must-visit destination for those interested in Kerala's rich cultural heritage and royal history.

**Architectural Splendor**

Kuthiramalika Palace is a stunning example of traditional Kerala architecture, showcasing intricate woodwork, detailed carvings, and elegant design. The palace is constructed primarily of teakwood, rosewood, marble, and granite, reflecting the opulence and craftsmanship of the era.

The palace's name, Kuthiramalika, derives from the 122 carved wooden horses that decorate the eaves of the structure. These exquisite carvings are a testament to the skill and artistry of the craftsmen of that time. The palace features typical Kerala architectural elements such as sloping tiled roofs, overhanging eaves, and spacious courtyards. These design elements not only enhance the aesthetic appeal but also provide natural ventilation and protection from the monsoon rains.

The interiors of the palace are adorned with intricate wooden carvings and traditional motifs. The ceilings, beams, and pillars are meticulously carved with floral patterns, mythological figures, and scenes from Hindu epics, showcasing the richness of Kerala's artistic heritage. The palace comprises numerous halls and rooms, each with its unique design and purpose. The grand halls are used for royal ceremonies and gatherings, while the smaller rooms served as living quarters for the royal family.

**Royal Artifacts and Museum**Kuthiramalika Palace is not just an architectural marvel but also a repository of royal artifacts and historical treasures. The palace has been converted into a museum that houses a fascinating collection of items that offer insights into the royal life and culture of Travancore. The museum displays several thrones, including the famous ivory throne used by the Maharajas of Travancore. The intricately designed wooden and ivory furniture reflects the luxury and elegance of the royal court.

Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma, the builder of the palace, was not only a ruler but also a renowned musician and composer. The museum exhibits a collection of traditional musical instruments used by the Maharaja, including veenas, mridangams, and flutes. The walls of the palace are adorned with paintings and portraits of the Travancore royal family and notable personalities of the time. These artworks provide a glimpse into the history and lineage of the royal family. The museum features an array of antiques, including ancient manuscripts, ceremonial costumes, jewelry, weapons, and other artifacts that offer a deeper understanding of the cultural and historical heritage of Kerala.

**Cultural Significance and Events**

Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a historical monument but also a vibrant cultural center that hosts various events and programs:

**_Swathi Sangeethotsavam:_**This annual music festival, held in January, commemorates the birth anniversary of Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma. The festival attracts renowned classical musicians and performers from across India, who come to pay tribute to the musical legacy of the Maharaja. The palace courtyard serves as the venue for these performances, creating a magical atmosphere that resonates with the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

_**Heritage Tours:**_ Guided tours of the palace are available, offering visitors a detailed understanding of its history, architecture, and the royal artifacts on display. Knowledgeable guides provide insights into the life and times of the Travancore royal family, making the visit a truly enriching experience.

**Accessibility and Accommodation**

Kuthiramalika Palace is easily accessible by road, being located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram city. The nearest railway station is Thiruvananthapuram Central, and the nearest airport is Trivandrum International Airport, both of which are within a few kilometers of the palace.

There are several accommodation options available in Thiruvananthapuram, ranging from budget hotels to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer modern amenities and are conveniently located near the city's major attractions.

Visitor Information: The palace museum has an entry fee, with different rates for adults and children. It is advisable to check the latest timings and entry fees before planning your visit.

Kuthiramalika Palace, with its stunning architecture, rich history, and cultural significance, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are exploring the intricate carvings, admiring the royal artifacts, or attending a cultural event, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal heritage of Kerala. A visit to Kuthiramalika Palace is not only a journey through history but also an opportunity to connect with the artistic and cultural essence of this beautiful region.

##### A historic site in Kerala, known for its gateway to Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple, royal palaces, and vibrant cultural heritage, including annual Navarathri celebrations.

East Fort in Thiruvananthapuram is a vibrant and historically significant area, renowned for being the gateway to the iconic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This bustling hub, filled with shops, commercial sites, and a steady stream of visitors, has witnessed the evolution of the city from the days of the Travancore Kingdom to the present day. Recognizing its historical importance, the State Government has declared East Fort a heritage site, preserving its cultural and architectural legacy.

As visitors approach East Fort, they are immediately struck by the imposing white gateway on the eastern side, which faces the famous Chalai Bazaar. This gateway, built in 1747 by King Marthanda Varma, is the most prominent of the fort's gates. Nearby, the Vettimurichakotta Gate is home to C.V.N. Kalari, a well-known school of Kalaripayattu, Kerala's ancient martial art form. Directly aligned with the East Fort gate stands the majestic Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple. This seven-storied temple, built in the traditional Kerala and Dravidian architectural styles, is dedicated to Lord Padmanabha, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. The temple is not only a place of worship but also a marvel of architectural beauty, attracting visitors from around the world.

One of the unique features near the temple is the Methan Mani, a distinctive clock with a man's face and two goats on either side, which adds to the charm of the area. The East Fort also has other significant gates, including Nariadachankotta, Padinjarekotta, and Azheekotta, each with its own historical relevance.

Inside the fort, visitors can explore various structures associated with the erstwhile royal family, including numerous palaces and buildings that showcase a blend of traditional and Western architectural styles. The Ananthavilasam Palace, built in 1880 by King Vishakam Thirunal, is a prime example of Baroque and Rococo architecture. Another must-visit site is Kuthiramalika, also known as the Horse Palace, named for the intricately carved wooden horses that adorn its upper floors.

The area is also home to the Navarathri Mandapam, which hosts the annual Navarathri celebrations. This ten-day festival is renowned for its music festival, which attracts prominent artists and musicians from across the country, making it a key cultural event in Thiruvananthapuram.

East Fort and its surrounding heritage sites offer a fascinating glimpse into Kerala's rich history, culture, and architectural splendor, making it a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists.

**Historical Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace has a history that spans several centuries, dating back to the early 18th century. The palace was originally built by the royal family of Travancore as a residential and administrative center. Over the years, it has been the site of significant historical events and has hosted many distinguished guests, including British officials and Indian royalty. The most notable historical figure associated with Kilimanoor Palace is Raja Ravi Varma, one of India's greatest painters. Born in 1848, Ravi Varma is celebrated for his pioneering work in Indian art, blending traditional Indian themes with European techniques. The palace remains a symbol of his artistic legacy and continues to attract art aficionados from around the world.

**Architectural Features**

Kilimanoor Palace is an exemplar of traditional Kerala architecture, featuring wide verandahs, spacious courtyards, and long corridors. The palace's red-tiled roofs and brilliant white walls add to its picturesque charm. The architectural design incorporates local materials like wood and laterite stone, reflecting the indigenous construction techniques of the time.

**Raja Ravi Varma Studio**

The Chitrashala studio, designed by Raja Ravi Varma and built around 1875, is a significant part of Kilimanoor Palace. The studio boasts large glass windows that flood the space with natural light, creating an ideal environment for painting. It houses a dusty, aged easel and other tools used by Varma. The serene and inspiring surroundings include views of the flowering garden and paddy fields, which influenced Varma's works.

**Cultural and Artistic Significance**

Kilimanoor Palace is not only a historical site but also a cultural hub that celebrates the artistic heritage of Kerala. The palace's association with Raja Ravi Varma adds immense cultural value, as his works played a crucial role in shaping modern Indian art. Varma's paintings are renowned for their depictions of Hindu mythology, portraits of Indian women, and use of vibrant colors and intricate details. The palace preserves his memory with prints of his famous paintings, photographs, and personal artifacts. The Kilimanoor Palace Trust continues to uphold Varma's legacy by maintaining the palace and organizing events to celebrate his contributions to art. The palace regularly hosts art exhibitions, cultural programs, and workshops, promoting the arts and preserving the legacy of Raja Ravi Varma. Visitors can explore the museum dedicated to his works, attend lectures on his contributions to art, and participate in activities that highlight the rich cultural heritage of Kerala.

**Accommodation**

There are several accommodation options available in and around Kilimanoor, ranging from budget lodgings to luxury resorts. Many of these establishments offer comfortable stays with modern amenities, providing a convenient base for exploring Kilimanoor Palace and the surrounding attractions.

**Visitor Information**

The best time to visit Kilimanoor Palace is year-round, as its indoor setting ensures that weather conditions do not impact the experience, making it ideal for sightseeing and exploring the palace at any time.

Hiring a local guide can enhance the visitor experience by providing detailed information about the historical and cultural significance of the palace. Guides can also offer insights into the life and works of Raja Ravi Varma and the architectural features of the complex.

Kilimanoor Palace, with its historical significance, architectural splendor, and cultural heritage, offers a unique and enriching experience for visitors. Whether you are an art enthusiast, a history buff, or a curious traveler, the palace provides a fascinating glimpse into the royal legacy and artistic traditions of Kerala. A visit to Kilimanoor Palace is not only an educational journey but also an opportunity to connect with the timeless beauty and cultural richness of Kerala's past.

About Us

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation is a not-for-profit institution that works to preserve and promote the artistic legacy of one of India’s greatest artists. Started by his great, great granddaughter Bharani Thirunal Rukmini Bayi Tampuran in 2015, the Foundation’s activities are ably guided and managed by an expert panel of external and internal advisors, in the field of art, history, conservation and industry.

The Foundation is the only institution in the world that works in the space of research, documentation, authentication and education with regard to Ravi Varma and his art works. The Foundation works with public and private museums, collectors and any collections that house or own works by this incredible artist.

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Significance of the logo

The name Varma is derived from the original Sanskrit word “Varman” which means “armour” or “protection” or “shield”. The name Varma came to be used to refer to a Chief or Protector of an exclusive clan. The members of this clan were the Kshatriyas. The ancient source from where the people who belonged to this clan is believed to have originated somewhere in Central Asia. A King from Southern India, notably present day Kerala, by the name of Varma also finds mention in the Mahabharata war.

Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation, with its new logo, embraces Varma or the Shield in an appropriate and distinct manner. The intent behind the Foundation’s logo is in keeping with our endeavour to protect his artistic legacy and the creative direction that Ravi Varma showed during his lifetime.

The presence of the Trident in our logo is significant in that it is an invaluable accessory to the protective armour or shield.

While we have embraced a new logo which is bright, bold and beautiful, our principles at the Foundation remain unchanged and firmly entrenched in Ravi Varma’s ideals. Our endeavour is to preserve and promote the rich legacy of one of India’s greatest artists.

- Rukmini Varma

_Chairperson, Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation_

[](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=http://www.rrvhfoundation.com/&h=AUC1FrlEHoasQeHnTur_q5GAW9i0OnaR_BYIBFLyXEpeHAhWJrBjYKTDw9-vMjmHvgznBKAWIUXOiKMlnWsiLXp1VCrZxv5cxfcn4KEkH4ZWHm0NlMEAE-TysINa5hPp35D2O5aTKkdKjNrmygf8XnO9leA#)

#### Our Objectives

Briefly, these are to:

1. Increase awareness of his work through lecture series, exhibitions, short films and books

2. Promote his legacy and document his influences on jewellery, textiles and on other artists, through exhibits and talks

3. Provide valid authentication for his original works created in oil

## Ab out Raja Ravi Varma

![Image 21](https://l.facebook.com/images/photos/about-img1.jpg)

The life and works of one of India's most prolific artists.

Raja Ravi Varma was a painter par excellence whose works not only put India on the map but also placed him on the pedestal with other great artists. Born 29 April, 1848 at Kilimanoor in the erstwhile State of Travancore, Ravi Varma’s paintings of the Royals, illustrious personalities and contemporary figures were widely sought-after and greatly admired.

An eye for detail, splendid use of colours and rich texture gave his paintings a classy, exquisite look, the reason why his works are priceless even to this day.

His realistic portrayals and interpretations of religious and mythological figures that adorn the households today, captivated and fascinated the country as well as an international audience.

Ravi Varma’s works transcended painting; he was also a poet, scholar and a visionary far beyond his times. His work also helped focus attention on his talented peers and paved the way for a succession of artistes.

Ravi Varma’s intention was to take art to the common man and not to limit it just to a privileged few. By establishing a press to make reproductions of his works, Ravi Varma ensured a strong foundation of admiration and respect from all.

Passing away on 2nd October 1906 at the age of 58, Ravi Varma’s legacy continues to live and thrive through his works and the Foundation.

#### His Influence

Over the years many of us have forgotten how Raja Ravi Varma has influenced our lives in subtle, yet defining ways. His visual images of gods and goddesses which attained celestial reverence has impacted almost all walks of life. These can be related to his influence on Indian comic books, temple architecture, jewellery, textiles and ceramics to name a few.

## Ev ents

![Image 22: Ram Sagar darp haran - A S Desai](https://l.facebook.com/images/portfolio/sri-rama-vanquishing-the-sea.jpg)

A brief calendar of events & exhibitions

Since inception in 2015, the Raja Ravi Varma Heritage Foundation has successfully conducted and executed several exhibitions, talks, panel discussions and even made a short film on Raja Ravi Varma's birth place, in its effort to preserve his legacy - both artistic and otherwise.

Some of our most popular events have been:

*   _**Foundation’s Season Five -**_ The fifth year of the Foundation will go down as one of the most memorable. Having earmarked five speakers for what has been our Season Five, the Foundation enlisted the services of five speakers, diverse, yet distinct in their field, to talk about Ravi Varma and his art.

The RRVHF brought on board noted Oxford-based Prof. Partha Mitter, art expert and Yale University lecturer Patrick Connors, noted historian and conservator Rupika Chawla. While the three of them are distinguished in their respective fields, the Foundation, in keeping with the diverse tune, roped in Dinesh Vazirani, CEO and Co-Founder of SaffronArt, one of the top international auction houses. Vazirani’s interactive session was primarily to give his insight on the Art of Investment and to decode the myths surrounding auction houses and its processes.

As the finale to Season Five, the Foundation organized a talk by Deepanjana Pal, journalist and author of The Painter: A life of Raja Ravi Varma. Her perspective on the master artist and his works are different, yet relevant and it gelled well with our theme of bringing in five varied speakers to disseminate their knowledge on Ravi Varma and his art.

All the talks have been uploaded on YouTube and those desirous of watching the talk again may kindly click on the YouTube icon or [here](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCke9w2FMmyc8FZJymov5Q5A) and watch the desired event in full.

*   _**Ravi Varma & His Contemporaries -**_ Historian and conservation specialist Rupika Chawla was in conversation with author Manu S Pillai on the influence of the great master on a generation of contemporary artists like Sekhara Warrier, Mukundan Tampi, Neelakanta Pillai and others. The Foundational also worked with a group of private collectors displaying 11 original oil paintings for the day at the Kerala Museum, Kochi.
*   _**Raja Ravi Varma: His Mythological Perspectives -**_ Devadutt Pattanaik kept the audience engrossed, dwelling on the huge role that Ravi Varma played in bringing the gods and goddesses and mythological characters closer to the common man during his lifetime, by way of his art. Pattanaik explained the mythological essence in some of Ravi Varma’s works like Dhruva Narayan, Ambika, Shankar to name a few.

The chronological detailed listing of the events can be found in the link below:

[Foundation Events](https://l.facebook.com/events.html)

These events, all planned and curated by the Foundation, shed light on the artist's impact on mythology, music, jewellery and textiles among others.

##### A historic palace in Thiruvananthapuram, built during the Travancore era, now serves as a cultural venue with notable architecture and India's first digital garden.

Kanakakkunnu Palace, located in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, is not only an architectural marvel but also a vibrant cultural hub. The palace, perched on a hillock, was believed to have been built during the 19th century under the reign of the erstwhile king of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal. Originally constructed to serve as a guest house, this red-bricked structure with white stone dressings is a fine example of Kerala-Gothic Victorian-era architecture.

The palace's design is both elegant and functional, featuring a dignified neoclassical entrance portico and a circular hall adorned with magnificent crystal chandeliers and exquisite pieces of royal furniture. The surrounding grounds are equally captivating, with meadows, groves, and flowering shrubs creating a serene atmosphere. The palace is also home to India's first digital garden, where visitors can scan QR codes to learn about the various plants, including their botanical names, species, nativity, and distribution.

Today, the palace serves as a popular venue for a multitude of cultural events, seminars, and programs. Its close proximity to other important tourist sites, such as the Napier Museum and Trivandrum Zoo, makes it an integral part of the city's daily life.

The palace grounds include two auditoriums—the Nishagandhi Auditorium, an open-air venue, and the Sooryakanthi Auditorium. The palace premises come alive during the all-India dance festival organized by the Department of Tourism, which runs from October to March. This festival attracts visitors from across the country who come to witness mesmerizing classical performances.

Kanakakkunnu Palace is also a popular meeting point for locals who enjoy its pleasant environment. In the evenings, the palace grounds buzz with activity as families and friends gather to unwind after a busy day.

With its unique blend of architectural beauty and cultural significance, Kanakakkunnu Palace remains a cherished landmark in Thiruvananthapuram, continuing to play a central role in the city's cultural and social life.

Shashi Tharoor arrived at the district collectorate this afternoon with senior party leaders

**Thiruvananthapuram:**
Senior Congress leader and three-time Lok Sabha MP Shashi Tharoor filed his nomination today from the Thiruvananthapuram constituency for the fourth consecutive time in the Lok Sabha elections.

Mr Tharoor arrived at the district collectorate this afternoon with senior party leaders, including MLA M Vincent, former minister VS Sivakumar, and Thiruvananthapuram district Congress chief Palode Ravi and other workers.

He shook hands with people and exchanged pleasantries on his way to the Collectorate complex. Some party activists draped shawls around him and expressed their support.

Before filing his nomination, Mr Tharoor prayed at the famed shrines in the constituency, including the Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple and the Pazhavangadi Ganapathi Temple.

With senior CPI leader and former Thiruvananthapuram MP Pannian Raveendran and BJP leader and Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar as his challengers, the high-profile constituency is set for a fierce three-cornered battle in the crucial polls.

Shashi Tharoor, a former UN diplomat, began his journey in electoral politics, winning Thiruvananthapuram in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls.

He scored a hat-trick in the 2019 general elections with a margin of 99,989 votes over his nearest rival.

Polling will be held on April 26 in Kerala for all 20 Lok Sabha constituencies in the state.

Thiruvananthapuram, formerly known as Trivandrum, serves as the capital of Kerala and is also a Lok Sabha constituency. Situated in the southernmost part of the mainland on Indias western coast, it is Keralas most populous city and a significant information technology hub. As of the 2011 census, the district had a population of 3,301,427. The Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency comprises seven assembly seats: Thiruvananthapuram, Kazhakuttom, Vattiyoorkavu, Nemom, Kovalam, Neyyattinkara, and Parassala. In the first election in 1951, under the name Travancore-Cochin, Annie Mascarene, an independent candidate and freedom fighter, emerged victorious. Since then, the seat has been a stronghold of the Congress party. In the 2014 elections, the constituency had 1,272,748 voters, with 614,438 males and 658,310 females. Shashi Tharoor, the Congress candidate, has been the wealthiest contestant from this seat. In the 2009 elections, Tharoor received 326,725 votes, followed by CPM candidate P Ramachandran Nair with 226,727 votes. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, Shashi Tharoor secured a hat-trick victory with 416,131 votes, while BJP candidate Kummanam Rajashekharan secured the second position with 316,142 votes. In the 2014 elections, Tharoor won again with 297,806 votes, followed by BJP candidate O Rajagopal with 282,336 votes and CPI candidate Bennet Abraham with 248,941 votes.

Tharoor, a former UN diplomat, has been representing the seat since 2009. Counting of votes in this constituency along with 19 remaining seats in Kerala began at 8 am. India Today Axis My India exit poll had predicted earlier that Chandrasekhar would have an edge over Tharoor. The Lok Sabha contest in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala's most populous city, has been primarily between the Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist), with the BJP gaining prominence in recent elections. In the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, Tharoor secured a hat-trick victory with 4,16,131 votes, while BJP candidate Kummanam Rajashekharan secured the second position with 316,142 votes. # How Shashi Tharoor won Thiruvananthapuram for the third consecutive time

BJP’s Kummanam Rajasekharan came second by a considerable margin of around one lakh votes in Thiruvananthapuram.

![Image 2: How Shashi Tharoor won Thiruvananthapuram for the third consecutive time](https://cf-images.assettype.com/tnm%2Fimport%2Fsites%2Fdefault%2Ffiles%2FTharoor-750.jpg?w=480&auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max)

How Shashi Tharoor won Thiruvananthapuram for the third consecutive time

Written by:

[Korah Abraham](https://www.thenewsminute.com/author/korah-abraham)

[](https://twitter.com/thekorahabraham)

Published on:

23 May 2019, 1:32 pm

*   [](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thenewsminute.com%2Fkerala%2Fhow-shashi-tharoor-won-thiruvananthapuram-third-consecutive-time-102293)

*   [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thenewsminute.com%2Fkerala%2Fhow-shashi-tharoor-won-thiruvananthapuram-third-consecutive-time-102293)
*   [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thenewsminute.com%2Fkerala%2Fhow-shashi-tharoor-won-thiruvananthapuram-third-consecutive-time-102293&title=How%20Shashi%20Tharoor%20won%20Thiruvananthapuram%20for%20the%20third%20consecutive%20time)
*   [](mailto:?subject=How%20Shashi%20Tharoor%20won%20Thiruvananthapuram%20for%20the%20third%20consecutive%20time&body=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thenewsminute.com%2Fkerala%2Fhow-shashi-tharoor-won-thiruvananthapuram-third-consecutive-time-102293)
*   Copied 

From exit and opinion polls to political pundits, predictions had indicated that a third consecutive victory would be an uphill task for the Congress in Kerala’s capital Thiruvananthapuram, considering the BJP had deployed a strong leader, Kummanam Rajasekharan, amidst their effort to unify the Hindu vote. But the people of Thiruvananthapuram constituency have revealed that they still prefer their sitting Member of Parliament and Congress leader, Shashi Tharoor.

While Shashi Tharoor polled over 40% of the votes – 4,11,525 out of 10,01,063 polled in the constituency – BJP’s Kummanam Rajasekharan secured the second position, with 3,13,339 votes. Communist Party of India’s (CPI) C Divakaran, who polled 2,55,625 votes (25.53%) votes came third in the race. Speaking to the media, Tharoor made a cricket analogy about his victory. "I feel like a batsman who has made a century while his team lost the match," he said to the media, referring to the Congress party's poor show at the Centre.

What has baffled political analysts in Kerala, many of whom had predicted a loss for Tharoor is that he has managed to increase his vote share from 2014. In 2014, even though Tharoor managed to win for a second consecutive term as the MP from Thiruvananthapuram, it wasn’t an easy ride. BJP’s O Rajagopal lost to Tharoor by a margin of just 15,470 votes, that is, by 1.64%. With the BJP’s campaign on Sabarimala reaching a crescendo, many had expected that the upper caste Hindu votes that Tharoor commanded would move to the BJP. It had been speculated that even if Tharoor was able to retain the coastal votes and minority votes, he would still not be able to offset the loss by erosion of votes to the BJP.

However, Tharoor has proved critics wrong by winning by a significant margin. In fact, of the seven Assembly segments that make up the Thiruvananthapuram Parliamentary constituency, his rival – BJP’s Kummanam Rajasekharan – has done better than him in only Nemom, which is the BJP’s only Assembly seat in Kerala.

![Image 3](blob:http://localhost/48f76619a5bd00ce057f2024dcf38bc1)

Shashi Tharoor celebrating his victory along with Congress leaders in Thiruvananthapuram.

The biggest shot in the arm for Shashi Tharoor was however the coastal vote – in the coastal Assembly segments of Neyyattinkara, Parassala, and Kovalam, Tharoor has a good lead over his rivals. The voters in these regions – Nadar and Latin Christians – have decided the fate of candidates for a long time, and Tharoor managed to get these votes.

In Kazhakoottam, Vattiyoorkavu, and Thiruvananthapuram Assembly segments where Tharoor had not performed well in 2014, he had a tough fight with Kummanam Rajasekharan this time around, winning by slim margins in each of the three segments. The significance of Tharoor’s victory this time is that he has not only raised his share in the coastal segments that protected him in 2014, but also wrested back the voters from the BJP in the other assembly segments. He is almost back to where he began in 2009.

J Prabash, retired professor of Kerala University and political analyst says that the minority vote has also consolidated in Tharoor’s favour. "It is important to note that there has been a consolidation of minority votes in favor of UDF. As far as the minorities were concerned, their aim was to keep the BJP out of power in the Centre as well as in the state. Also, various opinion polls had shown that in Thiruvananthapuram, Kummanam Rajasekharan might win and that C Divakaran would come in third place. This might have a threat to the minorities who voted for Tharoor to keep Kummanam out. Also, the Sabarimala issue had favoured the UDF in Kerala rather than the BJP,” Prabash said.

Shashi Tharoor is a two-time MP from Thiruvananthapuram, who was looking for a third consecutive victory. BJP’s Kummanam Rajasekharan is a popular BJP leader in the state as well as the former Governor of Mizoram, who resigned from the post in order to contest the elections. CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front’s (LDF) C Divakaran is a sitting Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) from the Nedumangad constituency in Thiruvananthapuram, as well as a former trade union leader.

Thiruvananthapuram was touted to be one of the constituencies from where the BJP would open its first Lok Sabha MP account, mostly because of its Hindu- majority demography, that’s much higher than the state average.

It is important to note that two-time MP Shashi Tharoor was an outsider to politics, let alone Kerala politics when he contested the Lok Sabha elections in 2009 from the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) ticket in Thiruvananthapuram. In 2009, Tharoor, polled 3,26,725 votes securing a vote share of 44.29%. He won after he defeated CPI’s P Ramachandran Nair by a margin of 99,998 votes. BJP’s PK Krishnadas came third that year, polling a total of 84,094 votes.

In 2014, Shashi Tharoor had secured a total of 2,97,806 votes, whereas O Rajagopal, who came second, secured a total of 2,82,336 votes. Meanwhile, CPI’s Bennet Abraham came third with a total of 2,48,941.

Thiruvananthapuram, formerly known as Trivandrum, serves as the capital of Kerala and is also a Lok Sabha constituency. Situated in the southernmost part of the mainland on Indias western coast, it is Keralas most populous city and a significant information technology hub. As of the 2011 census, the district had a population of 3,301,427. The Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha constituency comprises seven assembly seats: Thiruvananthapuram, Kazhakuttom, Vattiyoorkavu, Nemom, Kovalam, Neyyattinkara, and Parassala. In the first election in 1951, under the name Travancore-Cochin, Annie Mascarene, an independent candidate and freedom fighter, emerged victorious. Since then, the seat has been a stronghold of the Congress party. In the 2014 elections, the constituency had 1,272,748 voters, with 614,438 males and 658,310 females. Shashi Tharoor, the Congress candidate, has been the wealthiest contestant from this seat. In the 2009 elections, Tharoor received 326,725 votes, followed by CPM candidate P Ramachandran Nair with 226,727 votes. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, Shashi Tharoor secured a hat-trick victory with 416,131 votes, while BJP candidate Kummanam Rajashekharan secured the second position with 316,142 votes. In the 2014 elections, Tharoor won again with 297,806 votes, followed by BJP candidate O Rajagopal with 282,336 votes and CPI candidate Bennet Abraham with 248,941 votes.

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-itspc-3012918-2026-10-09 "Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early")

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

## [Highlights: TVK's Kumaravel wins by 20,040 votes](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/story/madurantakam-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-tvk-vijay-maragatham-kumaravel-aiadmk-kanitha-sampath-dmk-i-paranthamen-3012909-2026-10-09 "Highlights: TVK's Kumaravel wins by 20,040 votes")

Madurantakam Bypoll Results 2026 Highlights: TVK candidate K Maragatham Kumaravel has won the Madurantakam Assembly by-election in Tamil Nadu by 20,040 votes, with all 27 rounds of counting completed. She secured 74,048 votes, defeating DMK candidate I Paranthamen, who polled 54,008 votes. AIADMK's S Kanithasampath finished third with 47,450 votes. The bypoll was held on October 6, with Madurantakam recording a voter turnout of 86.26 per cent, according to final figures released by the Election Commission. The contest was seen as a test of the ruling TVK, led by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, while the opposition parties sought to win the reserved Assembly seat.

The 2027 Assembly elections will present distinct political challenges in Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur, with the BJP defending power in three states, the AAP seeking a second term in Punjab and the Congress looking to regain ground across several key contests.

In Uttarakhand, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami will lead the BJP's bid for a third consecutive term in the 70-member Assembly. The BJP is seeking to break the state's pattern of alternating power between the BJP and Congress. Development, the Uniform Civil Code and governance will be central to its campaign, while Congress is banking on anti-incumbency, particularly in the hill districts.

In Punjab, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann will seek a second term for the AAP after its sweeping 2022 victory, when it won 92 of 117 seats. Employment, farmers' concerns, welfare, law and order and state finances are likely to shape the contest. Congress remains the main challenger, while the SAD is rebuilding and the BJP is expanding its presence.

In Goa, Chief Minister Pramod Sawant will lead the BJP into another closely watched contest. The party has remained in power since 2012 and won 20 of the 40 seats in 2022. Its strength later rose to 28 after eight Congress MLAs crossed over. Alliances and defections are likely to remain important factors.

In Manipur, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh faces the challenge of leading the BJP into an election shaped by the aftermath of prolonged ethnic turmoil. The BJP-led NDA holds 51 of 60 seats. Security, rehabilitation, displacement, inter-community relations and restoring normal life are likely to dominate the campaign.

Devasish Sharma resigned from his job and received the BJP ticket just 25 days ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma was circumspect about a BJP victory in the Muslim-majority Assam seat. But it was Himanta's appeal and the BJP's organisational strength that proved the CM wrong.

## [Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-poll-result-akhil-gogoi-says-minorities-deserted-congress-seeks-reset-itspc-3013239-2026-10-09 "Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout")

The BJP is all set to win the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election by a margin of over 1.5 lakh votes, with the Congress languishing in the third spot. Raijor Dal leader and former Congress ally, Akhil Gogoi, called the party's defeat in a constituency with over 55% Muslim voters a tragedy for all anti-BJP forces.

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-itspc-3012918-2026-10-09 "Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early")

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

#### FAQ's

[How many seats are going to polls?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha#accordion-1)

A total of 543 Parliamentary constituencies will go to polls in the upcoming general election. Four states -- Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Odisha and Sikkim -- will vote in the Assembly election alongside the national polls.

[How many seats are there in the Lok Sabha?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha#accordion-2)

The Lok Sabha comprises 543 seats, with a maximum limit of 550 elected members as determined by the Election Commission. Article 81 of the Constitution specifies that up to 530 members will be elected from the states, 20 from Union Territories, and the President has the authority to nominate two members from the Anglo-Indian Community.

[How many Lok Sabha members are elected by the electors of the Parliamentary Constituency?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha#accordion-3)

Each electoral district picks a single representative. Before 1962, there were constituencies with both single and multiple representatives. The multi-member constituencies were eliminated in 1962.

[For how many Lok Sabha constituencies can a candidate contest?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha#accordion-4)

According to Section 33 (7) of the Representation of the People Act, an individual is allowed to participate in Lok Sabha elections as a candidate in up to two constituencies.

[How frequently are state elections held in India?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha#accordion-5)

State elections are held periodically in each state and union territory of India to elect members of the respective legislative assemblies. The frequency varies depending on the tenure of each state assembly. However, the Centre is now mooting the idea of holding simultaneous state and national elections. A panel, led by former President Ramnath Kovind, has been constituted to determine the feasibility.

The Election Commission of India, on March 16, announced that the 2024 Lok Sabha elections will be conducted in seven phases, spanning from April 19 to June 1. The results are scheduled to be declared on June 4.

Voting for the initial phase is set for April 19, followed by subsequent phases on April 26, May 7, May 13, May 20, May 25, and June 1. The tallying of votes will occur on June 4.

In addition to the Lok Sabha elections, the Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar also unveiled the polling schedule for Assembly elections in four states.

According to Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar, the decision to conduct the polls in seven phases takes into account various factors such as geographical conditions, festivals, exams, and other considerations.

An estimated 96.8 crore individuals are eligible to exercise their voting rights in the forthcoming elections, which will be held across more than 12 lakh polling stations.

#### The Big Picture

## [The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong](link_103)

Devasish Sharma resigned from his job and received the BJP ticket just 25 days ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma was circumspect about a BJP victory in the Muslim-majority Assam seat. But it was Himanta's appeal and the BJP's organisational strength that proved the CM wrong.

[![Image 3: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma with the BJP's Devasish Sharma at a rally ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. (PTI Photo)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-with-the-bjps-devasish-sharma-at-a-rally-ahead-of-the-nagaon-lok-sabha-09161566-16x9_0.jpeg?VersionId=MzJYUAOQqQbQCZO6izDArIR4BkfVU5pc&size=982:552)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-election-results-2026-devashish-sharma-ias-bjp-assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-3013397-2026-10-10 [link_103] "The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong")

#### Assam Lok Sabha By-Election

## [Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout](link_104)

The BJP is all set to win the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election by a margin of over 1.5 lakh votes, with the Congress languishing in the third spot. Raijor Dal leader and former Congress ally, Akhil Gogoi, called the party's defeat in a constituency with over 55% Muslim voters a tragedy for all anti-BJP forces.

[![Image 4: Akhil Gogoi's (left) Raijor Dal and the Congress, led in Assam by Gaurav Gogoi, parted ways in September. (File)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/akhil-gogois-left-raijor-dal-and-the-congress--led-in-assam-by-gaurav-gogoi--parted-ways-in-septe-090117749-1x1.png?VersionId=fDNcyBeZDkvwlRT0ef_mBppN9PKhkD3o&size=115:115)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-poll-result-akhil-gogoi-says-minorities-deserted-congress-seeks-reset-itspc-3013239-2026-10-09 [link_104] "Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout")

#### Highlights

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](link_105)

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

[![Image 5: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma with the BJP's Devasish Sharma at a rally ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. (PTI Photo)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/breaking_news/202610/assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-with-the-bjps-devasish-sharma-at-a-rally-ahead-of-the-nagaon-lok-sabha-091637698-1x1.jpeg?VersionId=trYE12akVnxa3zUw1tROf8fNJ0Dr1QpE&size=115:115)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-itspc-3012918-2026-10-09 [link_105] "Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early")

## [Is Congress the weakest link in INDIA bloc? What Mood of the Nation poll says](link_106)

#### The Big Picture

## [The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong](link_103)

Devasish Sharma resigned from his job and received the BJP ticket just 25 days ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma was circumspect about a BJP victory in the Muslim-majority Assam seat. But it was Himanta's appeal and the BJP's organisational strength that proved the CM wrong.

[![Image 3: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma with the BJP's Devasish Sharma at a rally ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. (PTI Photo)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-with-the-bjps-devasish-sharma-at-a-rally-ahead-of-the-nagaon-lok-sabha-09161566-16x9_0.jpeg?VersionId=MzJYUAOQqQbQCZO6izDArIR4BkfVU5pc&size=982:552)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-election-results-2026-devashish-sharma-ias-bjp-assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-3013397-2026-10-10 [link_103] "The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong")

#### Assam Lok Sabha By-Election

## [Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout](link_104)

The BJP is all set to win the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election by a margin of over 1.5 lakh votes, with the Congress languishing in the third spot. Raijor Dal leader and former Congress ally, Akhil Gogoi, called the party's defeat in a constituency with over 55% Muslim voters a tragedy for all anti-BJP forces.

[![Image 4: Akhil Gogoi's (left) Raijor Dal and the Congress, led in Assam by Gaurav Gogoi, parted ways in September. (File)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/akhil-gogois-left-raijor-dal-and-the-congress--led-in-assam-by-gaurav-gogoi--parted-ways-in-septe-090117749-1x1.png?VersionId=fDNcyBeZDkvwlRT0ef_mBppN9PKhkD3o&size=115:115)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-poll-result-akhil-gogoi-says-minorities-deserted-congress-seeks-reset-itspc-3013239-2026-10-09 [link_104] "Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout")

#### Highlights

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](link_105)

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

[![Image 5: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma with the BJP's Devasish Sharma at a rally ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. (PTI Photo)](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/breaking_news/202610/assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-with-the-bjps-devasish-sharma-at-a-rally-ahead-of-the-nagaon-lok-sabha-091637698-1x1.jpeg?VersionId=trYE12akVnxa3zUw1tROf8fNJ0Dr1QpE&size=115:115)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-itspc-3012918-2026-10-09 [link_105] "Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early")

## [Is Congress the weakest link in INDIA bloc? What Mood of the Nation poll says](link_106)

The latest India Today–CVoter survey reveals the BJP's continued dominance in national politics while the Congress struggles within the INDIA opposition bloc. The NDA maintains a strong lead as the opposition faces internal challenges ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.

#### Exclusive

## [Why don't you contest from Sambhal? Asaduddin Owaisi dares Yodi Adityanath](link_99)

Asaduddin Owaisi challenged Yogi Adityanath to contest from Sambhal and asked Akhilesh Yadav to fight from Gorakhpur. He said the BJP and Samajwadi Party were staging a political fight while avoiding substantive issues ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh election.

[![Image 3: Asaduddin Owaisi at the India Today Conclave South.](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/asaduddin-owaisi-at-the-india-today-conclave-south-294341199-16x9.jpeg?VersionId=NFgAgnu6ZhEFZ5_Rrz2x.wFTHMpI6pvx&size=982:552)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/story/asaduddin-owaisi-challenges-yogi-adityanath-to-contest-from-sambhal-before-up-polls-3015299-2026-10-12 [link_99] "Why don't you contest from Sambhal? Asaduddin Owaisi dares Yodi Adityanath")

#### Assembly Elections 2027

## [Support Ram to defeat Ravan: Revanth Reddy targets BJP at Goa rally](link_100)

At Goa's Goy Rakhonn Yatra, Telangana CM, A Revanth Reddy urged voters to back Congress in 2027 and likened the BJP to Ravan. He coupled the appeal with attacks on the BJP government over drugs, land and unemployment, while projecting Rahul Gandhi's wider fight against the Centre.

[![Image 4: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/story/revanth-reddy-goa-speech-bjp-ravan-congress-2027-election-3015170-2026-10-12 [link_100] "Support Ram to defeat Ravan: Revanth Reddy targets BJP at Goa rally")

#### The Big Picture

## [The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong](link_101)

Devasish Sharma resigned from his job and received the BJP ticket just 25 days ahead of the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma was circumspect about a BJP victory in the Muslim-majority Assam seat. But it was Himanta's appeal and the BJP's organisational strength that proved the CM wrong.

[![Image 5: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-election-results-2026-devashish-sharma-ias-bjp-assam-cm-himanta-biswa-sarma-3013397-2026-10-10 [link_101] "The Himanta magic in Nagaon that proved Himanta wrong")

#### Beyond News

## [Vijay's TVK increases tally by two. Will need Congress even if it wins rest](link_102)

With victories in Dharapuram and Madurantakam, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK has increased its Assembly tally to 109. However, even if the party wins all five seats awaiting bypolls, it will still need the Congress for the minority government's stability.

[![Image 6: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/story/tvk-vijay-tamil-nadu-cm-byelection-results-seat-increase-congress-alliance-itspc-3013390-2026-10-10 [link_102] "Vijay's TVK increases tally by two. #### Assam Lok Sabha By-Election

## [Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout](link_103)

The BJP is all set to win the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election by a margin of over 1.5 lakh votes, with the Congress languishing in the third spot. Raijor Dal leader and former Congress ally, Akhil Gogoi, called the party's defeat in a constituency with over 55% Muslim voters a tragedy for all anti-BJP forces.

[![Image 7: Akhil Gogoi's (left) Raijor Dal and the Congress, led in Assam by Gaurav Gogoi, parted ways in September](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/images/story/202610/one-sen-capton-with-both-names-on-the-allicnce-tootna-095819216-16x9_0.png?VersionId=9Q5et1zj2WdqOFCQYmtv_eiF_u66VuFL&size=982:552)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-poll-result-akhil-gogoi-says-minorities-deserted-congress-seeks-reset-itspc-3013239-2026-10-09 [link_103] "Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout")

#### Election 2026

## [BJP landslide in Assam, Bengal bypolls; TVK on top in Tamil Nadu](link_104)

Counting is under way in by-elections across Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Assam and Puducherry, with the BJP leading in Assam and West Bengal and TVK locked in a close fight with the AIADMK in Tamil Nadu.

[![Image 8: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/story/bypolls-counting-results-nandigram-rejinagar-nagaon-bjp-vijay-tmk-aiadmk-dharapuram-madurantakam-puducherry-3013030-2026-10-09 [link_104] "BJP landslide in Assam, Bengal bypolls; TVK on top in Tamil Nadu")

#### Assembly Elections 2027

## [AINRC's Ashok Anand beats Congress's Vinayagam by 8,482 votes in Puducherry bypoll](link_105)

The victory is significant for AINRC, an ally of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), as the bypoll was held in a constituency previously represented by Puducherry Chief Minister and AINRC founder N Rangaswamy.

[![Image 9: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/story/all-india-nr-congress-retains-thattanchavady-seat-as-ashok-anand-defeats-congresss-e-vinayagam-by-8482-votes-3013031-2026-10-09 [link_105] "AINRC's Ashok Anand beats Congress's Vinayagam by 8,482 votes in Puducherry bypoll")

#### Highlights

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](link_106)

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

[![Image 10: Bankipur Assembly by-election](https://akm-img-a-in.tosshub.com/indiatoday/dashboard/itprod/default_image.jpg)](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/lok-sabha/story/nagaon-by-election-results-2026-live-updates-bypoll-vote-counting-itspc-3012918-2026-10-09 [link_106] "Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early")

## [Minorities too have deserted Cong: Akhil Gogoi rips into ex-ally after Nagaon rout](link_103)

The BJP is all set to win the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election by a margin of over 1.5 lakh votes, with the Congress languishing in the third spot. The victory is significant for AINRC, an ally of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), as the bypoll was held in a constituency previously represented by Puducherry Chief Minister and AINRC founder N Rangaswamy.

#### Highlights

## [Highlights: BJP registers big win in Muslim-majority seat, Himanta says Diwali has come early](link_106)

If you have been following this blog, you kept yourself best-updated on the live results for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency of Assam. BJP candidate Devasish Sharma has registered a victory by a margin of around 1.4 lakh over AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal. The Congress, which fought to retain the Muslim-majority seat, was a distant third. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned and switched over to the BJP. Voting was held for the Nagaon seat on October 6, and the turnaround was about 76%. Just ahead of the counting, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said BJP might not win Nagaon seat, but Congress would be reduced to third spot. He would be happy he was proven wrong on the first, and right on the second. Shounak Sanyal and Sushim Mukul brought to you the updates throughout the day.

FAQ'S

## [What is an exit poll?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/exit-poll#accordion-1)

An exit poll is a survey based on responses collected from voters as they leave the polling booth after casting their vote.

## [What is the difference between an exit poll and an opinion poll?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/exit-poll#accordion-2)

An opinion poll is conducted before voting takes place, whereas an exit poll is conducted after the voting process.

## [How long are exit polls considered valid?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/exit-poll#accordion-3)

Exit polls are considered indicative only until the official election results are declared.

## [What are the Election Commission’s rules on releasing exit polls?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/exit-poll#accordion-4)

Releasing exit polls before the completion of voting in the final phase is prohibited by the Election Commission.

## [When will the Kerala Assembly Elections exit poll be released?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/exit-poll#accordion-5)

Exit polls are usually released on the evening of the same day after polling concludes.

Kerala Assembly Election FAQs

## [How many total seats are there in the Kerala Assembly?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-1)

The Kerala Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) has a total of **140 seats**. Public representatives are elected directly.

## [When will the Kerala Assembly Elections 2026 be held?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-2)

Voting for the Kerala Assembly Elections 2026 will take place on **April 9**, while the counting of votes will be held on **May 4**.

## [How many phases were the Kerala Assembly elections held in 2021?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-3)

The Kerala Assembly elections 2021 were conducted in **1 phase**.

## [When will Kerala election results be announced?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-4)

The Kerala Assembly election results will be out in the **first half of 2026**.

## [Which parties are mainly participating in the Kerala Assembly elections 2026?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-5)

The main parties in the Kerala Assembly elections 2026 are the **Left Democratic Front (LDF)**, **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, and the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, along with a few other regional parties.

## [What was the voter turnout in the Kerala Assembly elections 2021?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-6)

According to available data, the overall voter turnout in the Kerala Assembly elections 2021 was 74.06%.

## [What is the SIR (Special Intensive Revision) process?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-7)

SIR, or Special Intensive Revision, is a special process by the Election Commission through which names are added, removed, or corrected in the voter list.

## [How can I find the name of the winning candidate in my area?](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala/constituency-list#accordion-8)

You can check the name of the winning candidate in your area on the official website of the Election Commission: [https://results.eci.gov.in](https://results.eci.gov.in/). You can also check it on the India Today website: [https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala](https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/assembly/kerala)

## Kerala Assembly Election 2026 Schedule

The Kerala Assembly elections will be held in a single phase on April 9, 2026. The counting of votes will be done on May 4.

Assembly elections are scheduled to take place in four states and a Union Territory this year. While Assam, Kerala and Puducherry will go to polls on April 9, Tamil Nadu will vote on April 23 and Bengal will vote in two phases on April 23 and April 29. Results for all these states will be declared on May 4.

Alappuzha, considered a VIP constituency in Kerala, has alternated between sides, supporting both the Left Democratic Front and Congress. In the 2019 election, incumbent AM Arif won the only seat for the LDF. Renowned Congressman KC Venugopal also has a successful electoral history in Alappuzha. Although this parliamentary constituency has a communist legacy, it has mostly been a stronghold of the Congress. Alappuzha is famous for its tourism, especially houseboat cruises. Due to its proximity to the sea, agriculture and marine economy thrive here. In addition to handloom and marine products, the strongest industry here is jute production. This parliamentary constituency is also known as Alappi and it consists of seven Assembly segments. These are Aroor, Cherthala, Alappuzha, Ambalappuzha, Haripad, Kayamkulam, and Karunagappalli. This seat has been a stronghold of the Congress, although the Communist Party of India (Marxist) has given it a tough fight. In the first general elections held in 1951-52, independent candidate PT Punnoose defeated Congress candidate AP Udhayabhanu by nearly 76,000 votes. After that, this seat was won by CPI in 1957, 1962, and 1967, RSP in 1971, Congress in 1977, CPI(M) in 1980, Congress in 1984 and 1989, CPI(M) in 1991, Congress in 1996, 1998, 1999, CPI(M) in 2004, and Congress in 2009 and 2014. According to the Election Commissions data, in 2014, there were 6,11,877 male and 6,59,447 female voters in Alappuzha, with a total of 1,271,324 voters.

Polling for all the 20 Lok Sabha seats in Kerala took place in the second phase on April 26, 2024. Kerala saw a three-cornered contest between the BJP-led NDA, Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF).

In the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, the UDF emerged victorious in 19 out of the 20 seats. The lone seat secured by the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was in Alappuzha, won by the CPI(M).

The Attingal Lok Sabha constituency in Kerala came into existence after the delimitation in 2008. It includes the Assembly constituencies of Varkala, Attingal, Chirayinkeezhu, Nedumangad, Vamanapuram, Aruvikkara, and Kattakkada. Parts of Chirayinkeezhu and Mavelikara parliamentary constituencies have been included in it. Both these parliamentary constituencies have traditionally witnessed a close contest between the Congress and the CPI(M).

The constituency saw protests over the Sabarimala movement. The Attingal Lok Sabha constituency falls within the Thiruvananthapuram district. In Attingal, 66.46% of the population are Hindus and 19.10% are Christians. The number of Scheduled Caste people is 372,977. The literacy rate in the district is approximately 93%. The main source of income for the people of the district is farming.

**2019 Mandate:** According to the Election Commission, 74.24% voting took place in the Attingal Lok Sabha seat in 2019. Congress candidate Adoor Prakash won with 3,80,995 votes, defeating CPI-M candidate Dr A Sampath, who received 3,42,748 votes. BJP candidate Shobha Surendran received 2,48,081 votes.

**2014 Mandate:** In the 2014 elections, CPI(M) candidate A Sampath received 3,92,478 votes, securing roughly 45% of the vote. Congress candidate Advocate Bindu Krishna received 3,23,100 votes, BJPs S Girijakumari received 90,528 votes, and NOTA received 6,924 votes. A Sampath was elected as a Member of Parliament from the then Chirayinkeezhu seat in 1996. His connection to this area dates back to his fathers time. His father, A Anirudhan, recorded a historic victory over veteran Congress leader R Shankar from this area in 1967.

# ‘I’m a Modi Bhakt, won’t quit BJP’: R Sreelekha addresses resignation rumours

Former Kerala DGP, BJP state vice-president, and Vattiyoorkavu councillor R Sreelekha insisted that she had not quit the BJP and would remain in the party for life.
